item.title: NEC Endorses 90-Day Economic Plan To Ease Cost Of Living For Nigerians
item.description: The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate the gains of President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, with a focus on reducing the cost of living and improving food affordability. The plan also prioritises attracting investment, removing bottlenecks to economic activities and accelerating the completion of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians. According to a statement by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications in the Office of the Vice President, the endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, at NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually on Thursday and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. The five priority areas identified in the plan are food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. 161st NEC meeting on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting on the utilisation of proceeds from fuel subsidy removal. Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about progress under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery. He identified reducing headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions. The presentation also highlighted the need to translate macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment. Addressing Council members, Shettima said that although President Tinubu’s economic reforms were designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels must ensure that the objectives translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. He charged state governors and relevant institutions to focus on affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security. “The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said. Shettima described the Council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform and livestock development as critical to determining the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. item.content:encoded: The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate the gains of President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, with a focus on reducing the cost of living and improving food affordability. The plan also prioritises attracting investment, removing bottlenecks to economic activities and accelerating the completion of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians. According to a statement by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications in the Office of the Vice President, the endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, at NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually on Thursday and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. The five priority areas identified in the plan are food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. 161st NEC meeting on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting on the utilisation of proceeds from fuel subsidy removal. Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about progress under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery. He identified reducing headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions. The presentation also highlighted the need to translate macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment. Addressing Council members, Shettima said that although President Tinubu’s economic reforms were designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels must ensure that the objectives translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. He charged state governors and relevant institutions to focus on affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security. “The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said. Shettima described the Council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform and livestock development as critical to determining the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency “Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” he said, stressing that Nigeria’s federal structure should strengthen cooperation rather than hinder the delivery of essential services. On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the Vice President urged state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would ease the financial burden on commuters. He said the programme’s success should be measured by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed. “The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said. Shettima urged governors to bring their knowledge of local conditions into national policy decisions, adding that effective implementation required clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government. “Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each Governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said. He added that every policy proposal should be assessed by its ability to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government. “Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” he said. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC Reviews Ebola Response, Tasks States On Preparedness Meanwhile, NEC received an update from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory. Pate allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring Council members that Nigeria had the institutional capacity to contain the situation. He outlined efforts by the ministry and relevant stakeholders to establish a robust national response system, identifying coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and strategic communication as critical components. The minister said 21 state governments had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to establish appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms without delay. NEC Directs States To Strengthen Polio Eradication Efforts Council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya. It resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC stressed the need for timely release of counterpart funds, stronger routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to improve coverage in subsequent campaigns. It also emphasised that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to eradicating polio in Nigeria. NEC Moves To Unlock Livestock Sector’s Economic Potential On livestock development, Council received the report of its Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris. NEC acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country. It noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the Federal Government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between federal and state governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential. FG, States To Establish Joint Financing Framework For CNG, Electric Vehicles Council also considered a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed. It resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the Federal and State Governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country. NEC directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles. It also resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares. item.title: Ministers spend billions to secure appointments, APC spokesman alleges
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently focus on recovering the money. Hassan made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday, describing ministers as among the most corrupt officials in government and claiming the practice predates the APC administration. “Every time a government goes out, the most criminal elements in government are ministers,” he said. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed.” “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he said. “The biggest fraudulent people you arrest after every government are ministers.” He also questioned the role of ministers in budget implementation, arguing that the government’s ability to fund approved budgets should be a priority. “Why do we need ministers? Why do we need budget to be given to ministers?” he asked. ‘Power has improved under Tinubu’ Hassan also defended President Bola Tinubu’s performance, saying the administration had taken steps to address challenges in the power sector. He claimed Tinubu had approved more than ₦4tn for electricity meters, arguing that expanding household metering was important to improving electricity supply. “There is no way you fix power issue without having every household powered,” Hassan said. On the use of solar power at the Presidential Villa, Hassan said the government had introduced financing support to help civil servants acquire solar systems. “That is why he [President Tinubu] introduced Credicorp for civil servants to buy their own solar system,” he said. Tinubu will get votes in the north in 2027 Speaking on the 2027 general election, Hassan argued that President Tinubu’s projects in parts of the North would help him win in states such as Bauchi and Kano, where he lost in the 2023 election. “In 2023, Asiwaju was a candidate and not the president. He’s done a lot in places like Kano and done a lot of streets in the North that will translate to votes,” he said. Hassan also cited the renovation of 287 primary schools and more than 4,000 classrooms through the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) as examples of the administration’s achievements. The post Ministers spend billions to secure appointments, APC spokesman alleges appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Real Madrid forward target tipped for future La Liga move: ‘Has that dream’
item.description: Real Madrid forward target tipped for future La Liga move: ‘Has that dream’ Real Madrid have built some of their best eras on the foundation of signing Galacticos for huge money and making them work within a system. The club currently has many superstars like Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande. Now, according to journalist Matteo Moretto, one other player on Los Blancos ‘ radar, Erling Haaland, could eventually move to Spain to continue his career. Moretto believes Haaland will eventually play in Spain Speaking during MARCA ‘s special Los 100 de MARCA by Orange programme , Moretto suggested that playing in La Liga remains an ambition for the Norway international. “Haaland has always chosen his next destination step by step, considering the sporting aspect,” Moretto explained. “He’s winning and has won a lot. I think his next step will be La Liga.” Erling Haaland has performed really well in the Premier League. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images) The journalist then offered further insight into the striker’s ambitions. “We still need to see which team, but he would really like to play in La Liga. Haaland has that dream.” Moretto concluded with a confident prediction: “From what I hear, sooner or later he’ll end up in Spain.” His comments arrive at a time when there is a lot of uncertainty surrounding the legal proceedings involving Manchester City. Madrid have monitored Haaland for years and could explore a move for him if he becomes available in the summer of 2027. Could Haaland fit into Real Madrid’s plans? How do Real Madrid fit Haaland into the setup?. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Any club would love to have Haaland, but making him work within the system will be a major challenge. Haaland is among Europe’s most prolific goalscorers, offering exceptional penalty-box movement, physical presence and clinical finishing. His arrival would give Mourinho a traditional centre-forward capable of converting the chances created by Madrid’s attacking midfielders. However, Los Blancos ‘ forward line already features Mbappe, Vinicius and Diomande, and adding Haaland to the mix could be overkill. Financial considerations also matter, given the striker’s long-term Manchester City contract and the likely cost of any transfer. If the Norwegian eventually decides to pursue his Spanish ambition, Real Madrid will have to be all over it, and it remains to be seen how things pan out.

item.title: Remembering Kaziu Deyna: City's Polish pioneer
item.description: Remembering Kaziu Deyna: City's Polish pioneer On this day in 1947, a Manchester City pioneer and one of post-war Europe’s most gifted attacking midfield talents was born. Kaziu Deyna was a the Polish footballing legend. Though injury meant that he only played 43 times for the Club during his short stay in Manchester, Deyna was one of the early trailblazers for the thousands of overseas players who have subsequently brought so much to our domestic game. It’s easy to forget now but the arrival at Maine Road of the quiet, unassuming man from Starogard Gdanski made international headlines back in 1978. Kaziu arrived at the Club following that year’s World Cup finals in Argentina armed with a reputation for being one of the European football’s most accomplished dynamic midfielders. CITY+ | Sign up to access exclusive content A gold medallist at the 1972 Olympic Games and a silver medal winner at the 1976 Games, Deyna had also finished third in the 1974 Ballon d’Or award, behind Johan Cruyff and Franz Beckenbauer. He was the mainstay of the Poland side which shone at both the 1974 and 78 World Cup finals and was the first true European superstar to join City’s ranks. Though he had just turned 31, Malcolm Allison and Tony Book identified Deyna as a player who could add a touch of finesse to an already-strong squad. But given that this was in the days of the Iron Curtain with Poland part of the Eastern Bloc, in order to secure his capture there was red tape to cut through – and plenty of it. Deyna was still a captain in the Polish army and City had to first secure his release from military service, then secure a deal with his club Legia. The clubs agreed a fee of around £100,000 but the Polish side weren’t interested in a straight cash deal as such – instead, they wanted electronic hardware, such as photocopiers, printers and the like. It was unconventional to say the least, but City, then sponsored by electronics giant Brother, agreed and paid the transfer fee in state-of-the-art hardware. It wasn’t until November 1978 that the graceful Pole finally signed for City, but it proved to be the start of what was to be a largely frustrating stay in Manchester. Deyna wasn’t match-fit when he arrived, and it was a further fortnight before he made his league debut at home to Ipswich Town. His appearance added around 6,000 to the Maine Road gate, but City lost 2-1 to Bobby Robson’s side. The Pole was unfortunate to have arrived at the start of what would be a long, steady decline of City that would stretch for more than two decades, though the more immediate slump in form was all that mattered at the time. City would fail to win in 15 and Deyna’s injury woes meant by mid-March he had made just two appearances and it wasn’t until the final eight games of the campaign that he returned to the side fully fit and made a genuine impact. item.content:encoded: Remembering Kaziu Deyna: City's Polish pioneer On this day in 1947, a Manchester City pioneer and one of post-war Europe’s most gifted attacking midfield talents was born. Kaziu Deyna was a the Polish footballing legend. Though injury meant that he only played 43 times for the Club during his short stay in Manchester, Deyna was one of the early trailblazers for the thousands of overseas players who have subsequently brought so much to our domestic game. It’s easy to forget now but the arrival at Maine Road of the quiet, unassuming man from Starogard Gdanski made international headlines back in 1978. Kaziu arrived at the Club following that year’s World Cup finals in Argentina armed with a reputation for being one of the European football’s most accomplished dynamic midfielders. CITY+ | Sign up to access exclusive content A gold medallist at the 1972 Olympic Games and a silver medal winner at the 1976 Games, Deyna had also finished third in the 1974 Ballon d’Or award, behind Johan Cruyff and Franz Beckenbauer. He was the mainstay of the Poland side which shone at both the 1974 and 78 World Cup finals and was the first true European superstar to join City’s ranks. Though he had just turned 31, Malcolm Allison and Tony Book identified Deyna as a player who could add a touch of finesse to an already-strong squad. But given that this was in the days of the Iron Curtain with Poland part of the Eastern Bloc, in order to secure his capture there was red tape to cut through – and plenty of it. Deyna was still a captain in the Polish army and City had to first secure his release from military service, then secure a deal with his club Legia. The clubs agreed a fee of around £100,000 but the Polish side weren’t interested in a straight cash deal as such – instead, they wanted electronic hardware, such as photocopiers, printers and the like. It was unconventional to say the least, but City, then sponsored by electronics giant Brother, agreed and paid the transfer fee in state-of-the-art hardware. It wasn’t until November 1978 that the graceful Pole finally signed for City, but it proved to be the start of what was to be a largely frustrating stay in Manchester. Deyna wasn’t match-fit when he arrived, and it was a further fortnight before he made his league debut at home to Ipswich Town. His appearance added around 6,000 to the Maine Road gate, but City lost 2-1 to Bobby Robson’s side. The Pole was unfortunate to have arrived at the start of what would be a long, steady decline of City that would stretch for more than two decades, though the more immediate slump in form was all that mattered at the time. City would fail to win in 15 and Deyna’s injury woes meant by mid-March he had made just two appearances and it wasn’t until the final eight games of the campaign that he returned to the side fully fit and made a genuine impact. By that point, we were in real danger of relegation, but Deyna would prove pivotal in helping City survive. His late stooping header against Middlesbrough was his first goal for City and by the end of the campaign, he’d bagged six goals in six games and helped City avoid the drop. Against Aston Villa in the final match of the season, he bent a free-kick over the wall into the top corner of the net and received a rapturous ovation from the Maine Road fans. Deyna had the ability to always seem to have time on the ball and he had a grace and poise all-too-rarely seen on these shores at that time when the number of overseas players could be counted on one hand. The City fans loved him because he was capable of playing beautiful football and there were great expectations for his second season at Maine Road. Sadly, injuries disrupted the 1979/80 campaign for Deyna who would play just 21 times, scoring six goals. When he did get into his stride, he scored goals and also made them for team-mates. A stunning volley against Borussia Monchengladbach in the second leg of City’s UEFA Cup quarter-final showcased his ability, but question marks were raised about his fitness. With Tony Book and Malcolm Allison sacked in October 1980, John Bond took over and within a short space of time, Deyna was on his way out of Maine Road and off to North America where he joined the San Jose Earthquakes. He appeared, briefly, in the 1981 movie ‘Escape to Victory’ alongside the likes of Mike Summerbee, Pele, Sylvester Stallone and Michael Caine. He was one of the pioneers for the legions of overseas footballers that would follow, though he remains the only Polish player to have played for City. Tragically, Kaziu died in a car crash on September 1, 1989 in San Diego California. He was only 41-years-old. There was no doubting that he was a world class talent, and he is still adored in his homeland as one of Poland’s greatest ever stars even today. Former club Legia Warsaw later retired Deyna’s No.10 shirt in his honour and in 1994, a Polish Football Association and Polish sports newspaper poll voted Kaziu the greatest Polish player of all time, a fitting tribute to a special talent.

item.title: Kenny Atkinson admits Cavaliers were ‘depressed’ after LeBron James chose 76ers
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Kenny Atkinson has admitted the Cleveland Cavaliers were left “depressed” after LeBron James chose the Philadelphia 76ers over a potential reunion with his former team. The Cavaliers coach revealed that Cleveland had been anticipating James’ arrival and was excited about the possibility of working with the NBA superstar again. Instead, James joined Philadelphia, leaving Atkinson to come to terms with missing out on a player he had hoped to bring into his plans. Kenny Atkinson opens up on Cleveland Cavaliers missing out on LeBron James Speaking to ESPN’s Dave McMenamin, Atkinson described the disappointment of expecting a free-agent move to happen before learning that it would not. He said: “We were anticipating and excited to land LeBron and then you have that news, having gone through free agency a lot, when you’re expecting something to happen and it doesn’t happen, that first day or two, you’re just like, you’re depressed, quite honestly.” “That’s the emotions of it,” Atkinson added. His comments offer a glimpse into the Cavaliers’ hopes of bringing James back to Cleveland. However, his admission does not confirm how close the franchise came to completing a deal. For Philadelphia, James’ decision represents a significant addition, but the Sixers still need to turn their roster into a team capable of competing consistently. The early signs have been encouraging. Philadelphia rallied from 29 points down to beat Cleveland 114-106 in its home opener, giving Atkinson an immediate reminder of what his former target can bring to another team. James finished with 17 points and 10 rebounds, while Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 32 points. Joel Embiid also contributed 24 points in the comeback victory. The result added another layer to Atkinson’s disappointment, with James helping Philadelphia overcome the very team that had hoped to secure his services. However, one win does not settle the bigger questions surrounding the Sixers’ season. James’ experience and production will be important, but Philadelphia must build on that performance if it wants to make its recruitment count. For Cleveland, Atkinson’s comments reveal just how much excitement surrounded the possibility of a reunion. For the Sixers, the priority now is ensuring James’ arrival delivers more than an offseason headline. item.title: Netanyahu orders army to prepare for full West Bank closure after attack
item.description: The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the army to prepare for a full closure of the occupied West Bank Friday after Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched a "terror attack" near the city of Hebron. Emergency services said five people were injured and evacuated to hospitals.

item.title: Naomi Ackie Was Anything but Basic in Sculptural Schiaparelli at Paris Fashion Week
item.description: Naomi Ackie Naomi Ackie has been delivering some serious fashion moments lately, and her appearance at the Schiaparelli show during Paris Fashion Week is another one for the books. The British-Grenadian actress wore a striking black, single-sleeved gown that perfectly captured the house’s surrealist sensibility. Thousands of finely worked pleats created an almost liquid effect, hugging her figure before falling into a dramatic thigh-high slit. But what really makes this look special is the exaggerated sleeve, which gives the otherwise sleek silhouette an architectural quality. Naomi has worn the brand a few times, and we love how she always embraces the brand’s aesthetic without letting it overwhelm her. The sculptural statement earrings and signature face-motif clutch brought just the right amount of the house’s eccentricity, while her slicked-back ponytail kept the overall look sharp and modern. item.title: Dybala’s condition improves, Argentine aims return vs Cagliari
item.description: Dybala’s condition improves, Argentine aims return vs Cagliari Paulo Dybala is ready to return to the field. The Argentine striker underwent further checks yesterday afternoon on his slightly injured right calf, which is causing him almost no pain. The tests revealed a substantial improvement in his clinical condition. This news is a source of joy for the number 21, who is eager to return to the spotlight, and for Gasperini. The Giallorossi coach has been without Pellegrini for approximately two to three months and needs players in the attacking midfield to best support Malen. Paulo Dybala’s return is getting closer and closer. As reported by Corriere dello Sport, the number 21 could be on the bench for Roma-Cagliari, scheduled for Tuesday at 8:45 PM, and perhaps even come on for a few minutes. The Argentine striker’s initial target was the match in Udine, but there’s optimism he could start slightly earlier. If he were to come off the bench, even late on, Dybala would have a good chance of starting against Runjaić’s side.

item.title: 2027 Winter Series calendar: Three series across five circuits
item.description: Motorsport photo Gedlich Racing has presented the calendar for the 2027 Winter Series. From January to March 2027, the GT Winter Series, the GT4 Winter Series and the Formula Winter Series will be held across six dates at five different circuits in Spain and Portugal. One highlight of the programme is the 6 Hours of Portimao, which takes place at the start of February. The offering is aimed at different groups of participants. While the GT series are aimed at drivers and teams in GT racing, the Formula Winter Series gives up-and-coming Formula 4 drivers the opportunity to log race mileage before the start of the regular season. In addition, supplementary test sessions are planned. GT Winter Series for professionals and amateurs The GT Winter Series brings together various GT cars and drivers with different levels of experience. In addition to ambitious amateur and gentleman drivers, experienced drivers and professional teams can also take part. The focus is on competition on track and preparation for the rest of the season. The events give teams the opportunity to set up their cars under race conditions and prepare the drivers for the tasks ahead over the course of the year. GT4 Winter Series under SRO licence The GT4 Winter Series forms its own platform for GT4-category cars and is held under an official SRO licence. Technical checks and a Balance of Performance (BoP) are intended to create the conditions for comparable competition. Die GT4-Winter-Series fährt unter offizieller SRO-Lizenz Die GT4-Winter-Series fährt unter offizieller SRO-Lizenz The field is aimed at young drivers, experienced amateurs and Pro-Am line-ups. For young drivers, the focus is on building experience in GT racing. Established drivers and teams can use the races to improve their procedures and prepare for the coming season. Formula Winter Series with new format The Formula Winter Series is aimed at drivers in Formula 4. It enables young drivers to measure themselves against international competition under competitive conditions at the start of the year. For 2027, Gedlich Racing has announced a new tournament format with a limited number of cars per race. Participants are set to qualify for the concluding Masters Race via heats. In addition, a separate Contenders Race is planned, in which further drivers can fight for podium places. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Gedlich Racing has presented the calendar for the 2027 Winter Series. From January to March 2027, the GT Winter Series, the GT4 Winter Series and the Formula Winter Series will be held across six dates at five different circuits in Spain and Portugal. One highlight of the programme is the 6 Hours of Portimao, which takes place at the start of February. The offering is aimed at different groups of participants. While the GT series are aimed at drivers and teams in GT racing, the Formula Winter Series gives up-and-coming Formula 4 drivers the opportunity to log race mileage before the start of the regular season. In addition, supplementary test sessions are planned. GT Winter Series for professionals and amateurs The GT Winter Series brings together various GT cars and drivers with different levels of experience. In addition to ambitious amateur and gentleman drivers, experienced drivers and professional teams can also take part. The focus is on competition on track and preparation for the rest of the season. The events give teams the opportunity to set up their cars under race conditions and prepare the drivers for the tasks ahead over the course of the year. GT4 Winter Series under SRO licence The GT4 Winter Series forms its own platform for GT4-category cars and is held under an official SRO licence. Technical checks and a Balance of Performance (BoP) are intended to create the conditions for comparable competition. Die GT4-Winter-Series fährt unter offizieller SRO-Lizenz Die GT4-Winter-Series fährt unter offizieller SRO-Lizenz The field is aimed at young drivers, experienced amateurs and Pro-Am line-ups. For young drivers, the focus is on building experience in GT racing. Established drivers and teams can use the races to improve their procedures and prepare for the coming season. Formula Winter Series with new format The Formula Winter Series is aimed at drivers in Formula 4. It enables young drivers to measure themselves against international competition under competitive conditions at the start of the year. For 2027, Gedlich Racing has announced a new tournament format with a limited number of cars per race. Participants are set to qualify for the concluding Masters Race via heats. In addition, a separate Contenders Race is planned, in which further drivers can fight for podium places. Die Formula-Winter-Series startet 2027 mit einem neuen Rennkonzept Die Formula-Winter-Series startet 2027 mit einem neuen Rennkonzept With this division, the format is intended to take account of different performance and development levels within the field. For the young drivers, alongside race results, the focus is particularly on gaining experience on different circuits and preparing for the rest of the season. 6 Hours of Portimao as a standalone endurance race From 4 to 6 February 2027, the 6 Hours of Portimao is on the programme. In the standalone endurance race, teams will be challenged over a distance of six hours. Alongside speed, driver consistency, technical reliability, pitstops and race strategy also play an important role. The race will be held independently of the GT Winter Series and GT4 Winter Series championships. The Formula Winter Series will also be present in Portimao that weekend. Season on five circuits in Portugal and Spain The winter calendar takes participants to five circuits in Portugal and Spain. Alongside Portimao, Estoril, Jerez, Barcelona and Valencia are on the programme. In addition to the race events, test sessions are planned. They are intended to give teams the opportunity to work on car set-up, integrate new drivers and prepare for upcoming race outings. The 2027 Winter Series calendar: 14.01.-17. 01.2027: Portimao/Portugal (GT Winter Series, GT4 Winter Series) 21.01.-24.01.2027: Estoril/Portugal (GT Winter Series, GT4 Winter Series, Formula Winter Series) 04.02.-06.02.2027: Portimao/Portugal (6h of Portimao, Formula Winter Series) 11.02.-14.02.2027: Jerez/Spain (GT Winter Series, GT4 Winter Series, Formula Winter Series) 25.02.-28.02.2027: Barcelona/Spain (GT Winter Series, GT4 Winter Series, Formula Winter Series) 04.03.-07.03.2027: Valencia/Spain (GT Winter Series, GT4 Winter Series, Formula Winter Series) Information on the series, test sessions and registration at winter-series.racing . item.title: Beware the claw: Do you want to win the bunny or reboot Android?
item.description: Today's victim of the bork fairy is a claw machine that even Android seems to have rejected for its alleged unfairness. And Google, as we all know, is all about fairness. Eagle-eyed Register reader Scott spotted the stricken machine in an arcade adjacent to a roller rink, a place our reader visited with a friend and described as "something my currently bruised body reminds me I hadn't done for about 20 years." We assume they were talking about roller-skating, and not the exertions of accompanying their pal. The machine itself is a recent iteration of the infamous claw machine, which has spent a century emptying players' pockets in exchange for frustration and the very occasional reward of tat. Infamously, the devices are sometimes rigged so the claw's strength varies between turns, and in several parts of the world, gambling laws cover the machines. However, the only gambling to be done here is on whether or not Android will boot. Like so many players in the past, the machine has lost this bet, and an Android Recovery Console is on show. We're not sure who lennie022 is – perhaps a user or perhaps some corporate account – but the words "release-keys" probably don't belong on top of the device. They're unlikely to entice any everyday players to part with cash. The usual recovery menu is hidden thanks to the dimensions of the screen. If something like this comes up on a mobile device, the volume up and down buttons tend to be used for navigation. In this case, the joystick is presumably the only I/O method, and the selected option would be pot-luck. Which, we guess, is the whole point. More discreet is the screen below the machine which, rather than encourage a player to grip the sweaty handle, is now plaintively asking for some removable storage (we've seen enough electronic gizmos to know what those pictograms mean) on a blue background that would bring a tear to the eye of many a Microsoft engineer. In fact, something that looks a bit like a blue screen of death and a borked Android? Perhaps this combination would lure an engineer to the controls… Sure, there's no obvious place to stick removable storage or attach a keyboard. But a waggle of the joystick couldn't hurt, could it? Perhaps one more? Dammit. Now we're restarting Android, when all we wanted was that pink bunny. ®

item.title: Video: Bournemouth fans tease Amorim after another 3-0 loss
item.description: Video: Bournemouth fans tease Amorim after another 3-0 loss Ruben Amorim could only laugh as AFC Bournemouth fans serenaded him with a chant reminding him of a 3-0 defeat against the Cherries while head coach of Manchester United as Milan fell to defeat by the same scoreline in the Europa League on Thursday night. The Rossoneri were beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium on Thursday evening after goals from Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier and Amine Adli, the first two coming from the penalty spot. BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Tyler Adams of Bournemouth lies on the ground after a foul by Mike Maignan of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) Goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off for shoving Tyler Adams in the face prior to the second penalty, earning him widespread criticism in the Italian press on Friday morning. This result leaves Milan with just three points from their first three matches in the Europa League in 2026-27, which leaves them in 24th place in the standings. Towards the end of proceedings on Thursday night, the Milan head coach was treated to a chant of ‘Ruben Amorim, it’s happened again’ by the Bournemouth supporters, referring to a 3-0 defeat that Amorim had suffered while in charge of Manchester United back in December 2024. The Portuguese tactician let out a smile and a chuckle while the chant rang around the Vitality Stadium. Watch: Bournemouth fans tease Amorim during 3-0 Milan loss Ruben Amorim laughed off his warm welcome back to England 😅 pic.twitter.com/vTfLJGTDSc

item.title: ‘So humble’ – Fans show their appreciation as Lionel Messi answers how he wants to be remembered
item.description: Photo by CHANDAN KHANNA / AFP via Getty Images Lionel Messi’s playing career has been remarkable but at 39, it remains to be seen how long the Argentine has left. Messi has already retired from international football, playing the final game for his country earlier in October. He is now just focused on Inter Miami, where he is currently under contract until 2028. By that point the former FC Barcelona star will be in his 40s and it will be interesting to see if he decides to extend his deal or hang up his boots completely. Regardless of when he retires, Messi has now answered how he wants to be remembered. As quoted by Fabrizio Romano, he said: “A great athlete who always fought to achieve his goals and dreams. “Sometimes I succeeded in achieving what I wanted, sometimes I didn’t… but I never stopped trying to win everything that was in front of me” Many fans have now responded to that quote from Messi, praising him as a ‘humble’ player, sending their thanks and calling him the GOAT. One fan wrote: “The greatest to ever play the beautiful game of football and yet so humble.” Another responded: “He will always be remembered as the greatest on and off the pitch for eternity.” A third stated: “Thank you Leo for teaching us to never stay down, regardless how hard life tries to knock us down.” “Thank you so much sir GOAT,” commented a fourth, while another stated: “This is why Messi will always be the GOAT. Not just trophies, but that mentality. Never stopped trying even when he failed. From Rosario to World Cup champion, he fought for every dream. The greatest athlete of our generation.” A fifth tweeted: “‘Sometimes I didn’t.’ The man won literally everything and still talks like he’s chasing his first trophy. That’s Messi.” Another added: “‘Never stopped trying’ from the guy who literally won everything… that humility is why he’s the GOAT.” Messi is now set to return to action on Saturday in a meeting against the New York Red Bulls. item.title: Bayern Munich’s Jonathan Tah grateful for Vincent Kompany’s role in recent improvement
item.description: Bayern Munich's German defender #04 Jonathan Tah addresses the MD-1 press conference on the eve of the UEFA Champions League match between Viking and FC Bayern Munich at Lyse Arena in Stavanger, Norway on October 12, 2026. (Photo by Lise Åserud / NTB / AFP via Getty Images) / Norway OUT | NTB/AFP via Getty Images Jonathan Tah spent an entire decade at Bayer Leverkusen before deciding to do something different. Having joined Die Werkself in 2015, he left for Bayern Munich in 2025 and joined up with the Vincent Kompany-led Bavarians. The move has been a big success thus far, as he has carved out a role as the most-used center-back under Kompany in the 2025/26 season. As much as Kompany values Tah, though, Tah values him just as much. As a former center back, Kompany has been able to give Tah special attention and assistance in training, something Tah believes has made him a better player. “He has improved me a lot,” Tah explained in a recent interview with The Times (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “He’s someone who really sees the whole picture. Looks beyond the game, beyond the pitch. He’s really focused on developing the personality of a player and wants me to be a leader like he was. He’s so young, you watch how he handles things as a coach and sometimes feel he’s doing the same thing he would as a player. We’re convinced that with this identity, if we bring it, we can win every game.” Tah’s role within the team will continue to evolve and he seems to have made some strong improvements under Kompany. If he can keep that going, he could continue to be a vital piece of the Bayern Munich puzzle for the rest of this season (and hopefully longer). Join the conversation! item.title: Should Man Utd boss Carrick drop captain Fernandes?
item.description: Bruno Fernandes has scored 111 goals in 338 appearances for Manchester United [Getty Images] Michael Carrick is never short of advice around how he should do his job as head coach of Manchester United. Few of his players divide opinion quite so much as skipper Bruno Fernandes. So, it stands to reason there are a variety of views around whether Fernandes should be dropped for Sunday's vital Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Former Everton and Rangers striker Duncan Ferguson has no doubts. "It is a big problem for Michael," he told The Overlap podcast. "Put people in the team you trust. Your captain has thrown you under the bus. If you don't think he is playing for you, get him out. I wouldn't pick him even though he is their best player." Joe Smith, respected host of Manchester United fan channel Stretford Paddock, is of the same opinion. "I don't think Fernandes should play on the weekend," he said. "I don't think (Lisandro) Martínez should've played against Leeds, because otherwise they're running the ship here." United fans heading back on flights from Como to Manchester had a view, although much of it was wrapped up in their general thoughts about the club, most of which were negative. But only one man's opinion really counts. Carrick is the man who picks the team. His friend and former team-mate Wayne Rooney has a view on that. "When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart," he said on the United Stand podcast. "That was the start. We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility. "I was in that situation [as manager at Plymouth and Birmingham City] and if I was in Carrick's position now, I'd come out fighting. There's no more Mr Nice Guy." Fernandes was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee after 67 minutes of Manchester United's Champions League defeat in Como [Getty Images] Carrick is due to speak in a news conference to preview the Bournemouth game at 1330 BST. He will be asked whether Bruno Fernandes is going to be dropped. Many observers were shocked to discover Fernandes was not going to be disciplined for his post-match outburst following the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como. They were also surprised that he would remain as Manchester United skipper, when team-mate Lisandro Martinez was fined for attacking the club hierarchy eight days earlier after the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid. "It was an assassination," one source who has worked with Fernandes previously, told BBC Sport of Wednesday's comments. "It was unprofessional. Michael's team are killing him." item.content:encoded: Bruno Fernandes has scored 111 goals in 338 appearances for Manchester United [Getty Images] Michael Carrick is never short of advice around how he should do his job as head coach of Manchester United. Few of his players divide opinion quite so much as skipper Bruno Fernandes. So, it stands to reason there are a variety of views around whether Fernandes should be dropped for Sunday's vital Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Former Everton and Rangers striker Duncan Ferguson has no doubts. "It is a big problem for Michael," he told The Overlap podcast. "Put people in the team you trust. Your captain has thrown you under the bus. If you don't think he is playing for you, get him out. I wouldn't pick him even though he is their best player." Joe Smith, respected host of Manchester United fan channel Stretford Paddock, is of the same opinion. "I don't think Fernandes should play on the weekend," he said. "I don't think (Lisandro) Martínez should've played against Leeds, because otherwise they're running the ship here." United fans heading back on flights from Como to Manchester had a view, although much of it was wrapped up in their general thoughts about the club, most of which were negative. But only one man's opinion really counts. Carrick is the man who picks the team. His friend and former team-mate Wayne Rooney has a view on that. "When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart," he said on the United Stand podcast. "That was the start. We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility. "I was in that situation [as manager at Plymouth and Birmingham City] and if I was in Carrick's position now, I'd come out fighting. There's no more Mr Nice Guy." Fernandes was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee after 67 minutes of Manchester United's Champions League defeat in Como [Getty Images] Carrick is due to speak in a news conference to preview the Bournemouth game at 1330 BST. He will be asked whether Bruno Fernandes is going to be dropped. Many observers were shocked to discover Fernandes was not going to be disciplined for his post-match outburst following the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como. They were also surprised that he would remain as Manchester United skipper, when team-mate Lisandro Martinez was fined for attacking the club hierarchy eight days earlier after the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid. "It was an assassination," one source who has worked with Fernandes previously, told BBC Sport of Wednesday's comments. "It was unprofessional. Michael's team are killing him." The issue is whether Fernandes went too far in attacking Carrick's tactics for the Como game, then saying it was on the coaching team on the sidelines to spot the problem and change it, not the players. Fernandes is one of the most knowledgeable members of Carrick's squad when it comes to football tactics, and is desperate to succeed. His comments, made on TNT Sports weren't off the cuff, or said in an emotional state after a defeat, as Lisandro Martinez's were. Yet there is also sympathy for Fernandes from some at Old Trafford given the 32-year-old carried out 10 post-match interviews after the Como debacle, and also because, while hardly offering a defence of Carrick, the words were less inflammatory when they were spoken as they seem in text form. Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick apologised to the club's 700 travelling supporters for the 4-1 defeat at Como [Getty Images] It is easy to point to Sir Alex Ferguson, the former Manchester United manager who was a strong advocate of managers needing to have control over their players and wonder how he would have reacted to such a situation. Challenges to his authority tended to end with players leaving the club. However, you only need to listen to Gordon Strachan recounting instances from Ferguson's time in charge at Aberdeen on 'The Good, The Bad and the Football podcast' to accept some of the Scot's more extreme methods would not be acceptable in the current climate. Carrick must exist in the here and now. United's hierarchy are keen to get away from the cycle of sacking managers, having dismissed Ruben Amorim last season and Erik ten Hag in the one before. However, there is also a basic truth that Carrick desperately needs to end the present run of seven games without a win. If they fail against Bournemouth it would equal the sorry run of Louis van Gaal in 2015-16, which was the worst since a Ferguson-led side had eight draws and a defeat during the 1988-89 season. So, with Benjamin Sesko, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford all ruled out through injury, can Carrick drop Fernandes even if he wanted to? The Portuguese's link-up with Youri Tielemans has not flourished as imagined. And the only goal contributions by last season's PFA player of the year have been a hat-trick and assist in the 5-2 win over Ipswich in August and his strike against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK on 10 September. But, as Duncan Ferguson said, he is their best player. Carrick has to make the call. He needs to get it right. item.title: Maradona death trial verdict set for December 22
item.description: The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on December 22, the court announced Thursday, after six months of hearings. The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star’s death concluded Thursday with brief statements from Maradona’s daughter and some of the defendants. “I hope my father receives the justice he deserves…like anyone else,” said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion. The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona’s primary doctor, declared: “I am innocent.” Maradona died at age 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary edema. The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was found dead in his bed on November 25, 2020. He was at his residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence following minor neurosurgery. His death plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. – ‘Scapegoat’ – The trial, which began in April, included testimony from more than 70 witnesses. Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to twelve years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence — 12 years — sought for Luque. In closing arguments on Wednesday, Luque’s defense attorneys rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s death was foreseeable, calling their client a “scapegoat” in the case. Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated. His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters. “It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.” “I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said. The case has revolved around whether the doctors’ decision to allow Maradona to convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent. The prosecution pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or quickly available ambulance as evidence of what they presented as the defendants’ dereliction of duty. Several medical experts testified that Maradona’s caretakers failed to react to key warning signs — he was suffering from edema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing — in the lead-up to his death. The post Maradona death trial verdict set for December 22 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 'Napoli are not for sale' - Aurelio De Laurentiis reveals €3.5bn bid rejection and shuts down fresh takeover talk
item.description: SSC Napoli Presents New Head Coach Massimiliano Allegri - Getty Images Sport Napoli president Aurelio De Laurentiis has firmly dismissed renewed speculation that he is preparing to relinquish control of the Italian heavyweights following a recent meeting in the city. The veteran film producer also disclosed that he previously turned down a staggering multi-billion-euro proposal from Middle Eastern investors. Club chief dismisses buyout rumours De Laurentiis has reiterated that the Partenopei are staying in his hands after Corriere dello Sport reported a fresh meeting with Italian-American businessman Matt Rizzetta . Having rescued the bankrupt outfit in Serie C on September 6, 2004, the 77-year-old has overseen seven major trophies, including the 2022-23 and 2024-25 Serie A titles. However, recent talks with the Napoli Basket majority stakeholder reignited takeover rumours initially confirmed in May. Multi-billion approaches fail to tempt imago-sport-1080822141.jpg Under the Italian's 22-year stewardship, the southern giants also lifted the 2005-06 Serie C crown alongside three Coppa Italia triumphs (2012, 2014 and 2020) and two Supercoppa Italiana trophies (2014 and 2025). Clarifying his position during an interview on Radio Kiss Kiss via Sky Sport Italia on Thursday, De Laurentiis detailed his previous negotiations with Rizzetta's consortium and Middle Eastern suitors: "Napoli are not for sale. The Arabs offered me €3.5 billion, but I didn't want to retire. I still know how to make movies, and football, which I knew nothing about. I learned it despite countless difficulties. "About a year ago, I received a meeting request from Matt Rizzetta, whom I didn't know. I replied out of courtesy. He introduced me to a couple of funds he represented that wanted to buy Napoli. "This happened between February and March last year. We put their lawyers in touch with ours. We wanted to assess the proposal, including who was behind it, though we never actually began a due diligence process. "They wanted to pay part of the €2 billion upon signing and the rest over the following three years. Initially, I was told I would continue running the club, gradually scaling back my role until I eventually became honorary president. I asked for guarantees that the work we had done over 22 years of running the business would continue. I felt a duty to Napoli fans around the world. "Money matters, but it comes last. Matt Rizzetta told me he had two or three funds behind him, but the €2 billion would have come in over the years, rather than all at once." Local buyers preferred over Americans Back in May, the club supremo first addressed potential buyout approaches by stating: "The problem isn't money. It's whether a successor can lead with heart as well." Expanding on his latest catch-up with Rizzetta in Naples on Thursday, De Laurentiis added: "I'm happy to host him. The Arabs offered me €3.5 billion, but I didn't want to retire. I still know how to make movies, and football, which I knew nothing about. I learned it despite countless difficulties. "About a year ago, I received a meeting request from Matt Rizzetta, whom I didn't know. I replied out of courtesy. He introduced me to a couple of funds he represented that wanted to buy Napoli. "This happened between February and March last year. We put their lawyers in touch with ours. We wanted to assess the proposal, including who was behind it, though we never actually began a due diligence process. "They wanted to pay part of the €2 billion upon signing and the rest over the following three years. Initially, I was told I would continue running the club, gradually scaling back my role until I eventually became honorary president. I asked for guarantees that the work we had done over 22 years of running the business would continue. I felt a duty to Napoli fans around the world. "Money matters, but it comes last. Matt Rizzetta told me he had two or three funds behind him, but the €2 billion would have come in over the years, rather than all at once." Local buyers preferred over Americans Back in May, the club supremo first addressed potential buyout approaches by stating: "The problem isn't money. It's whether a successor can lead with heart as well." Expanding on his latest catch-up with Rizzetta in Naples on Thursday, De Laurentiis added: "I'm happy to host him. He hosted me in America to watch a basketball game. "When he brings up selling Napoli, I tell him not to get this soap opera going again. I want to build the stadium, and that will require a huge commitment, physically, too. He probably would have been happy with the Maradona. With a new stadium elsewhere, it would be wonderful to turn the Maradona site into a large park full of greenery. "For now, I haven't decided to sell, but if I did, I would prefer to sell to someone from Naples rather than an American. "We all know who we're dealing with on our own home turf. If someone from Naples wanted to take over from me in two, three, or five years, that would be fine. I have worked for 22 years for wonderful people." Stadium project dominates future plans SSC Napoli v FK Bodo/Glimt - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 Rather than entertaining foreign investment funds, De Laurentiis will now channel his energy into delivering a modern new stadium for the club away from the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Retaining full ownership ensures stability in the boardroom as the two-time recent Scudetto winners continue competing across Serie A and the Champions League. Any future handover will likely wait until a local Neapolitan buyer emerges over the next five years.

item.title: South Africa gripped by anti-migrant protests as foreign national is killed
item.description: Xenophobic unrest turns deadly in South Africa as a foreign national is beaten to death during a protest march in Durban, a city increasingly gripped by anti-migrant tensions. Meanwhile, as global efforts to raise awareness of lead poisoning intensify, teams in Ivory Coast go door-to-door testing homes for dangerous levels of the toxic metal. Finally, Ivorian authorities are cracking down on illegal mining over fears of pollution, but some young people say the activity remains one of their few sources of income.

item.title: Dani Olmo injury blow could hand highly-rated youth team star his first chance under Flick
item.description: Dani Olmo injury blow could hand highly-rated youth team star his first chance under Flick Barcelona midfielder Dani Olmo’s injury could finally open the door for Brian Farinas to earn his first competitive appearance for Hansi Flick’s first team, according to a report from SPORT , Notably, Farinas, 20, is waiting for an opportunity after remaining on the fringes of the senior squad despite being promoted from La Masia. Barcelona confirmed on October 21 that Olmo had suffered a left adductor injury and was expected to miss around a month, ruling him out of Sunday’s El Clasico against Real Madrid. His absence leaves Flick with another decision to make in the attacking midfield position. Farinas waits for his opportunity at Barcelona Farinas, who is in talks over a contract extension , has endured a difficult start to the campaign in terms of playing time. Brian Farinas could finally earn his opportunity. (Photo courtesy: X/FC Barcelona_es) While he has been registered with the first team wearing the number four shirt, he has yet to feature in a competitive match this season. Notably, Barcelona previously came close to allowing Farinas to leave for Girona during the summer, but Flick intervened and kept him at the club. The midfielder has continued working with the first team, with the German coach regularly offering guidance and correcting details to help him improve. Olmo injury opens door for Farinas Understandably, Fermin Lopez remains a leading option in the attacking midfield role, but Barcelona have several ways to cover Olmo’s absence. On that note, Pedri, Frenkie de Jong and Marc Bernal could operate in more advanced positions, while Lamine Yamal and Raphinha offer alternative tactical solutions. Barcelona want to renew Brian Farinas’ contract. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images) Farinas is further down the pecking order, but the injury could create a chain reaction that gives him an opportunity to earn minutes. His versatility across midfield could prove useful as Barcelona navigate a demanding schedule. As SPORT suggests, Farinas “will end up having his moment” . Flick “does not tremble when it comes to trusting La Masia” , and the Copa del Rey will provide further opportunities as the season progresses. For now, the next two months could be decisive. Farinas has no option to leave on loan in January at present, while Barcelona are also working towards extending his contract. His immediate priority, however, is to turn his patience into a competitive first-team opportunity.

item.title: Aurelien Tchouameni finally reveals what really happened with Valverde at Real Madrid: ‘Never came to blows with him’
item.description: Aurelien Tchouameni finally reveals what really happened with Valverde at Real Madrid: ‘Never came to blows with him’ Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni has revisited his altercation with Federico Valverde, insisting the pair never came to blows and revealing that the incident ultimately brought them closer together. Speaking on The Bridge (h/t AS ), the Frenchman addressed the controversy that overshadowed Real Madrid’s final weeks of the 2025/26 season. The incident occurred in May , with Valverde subsequently taken to hospital with a head injury. The club opened disciplinary proceedings against both midfielders before imposing a €500,000 fine on each player . Tchouameni denies reports of physical fight with Valverde Addressing the speculation surrounding the incident, Tchouameni rejected claims that the disagreement escalated into a fight. “People talk a lot, but there was no row between Valverde and me. Yes, it’s true that things happen in the changing room, but we never had a row. Tchouameni and Valverde were involved in a scuffle back in May. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “In a changing room there are digs and things like that, but I never came to blows with Valverde. It’s true that there was a bit of a nasty incident. “The only problem with all this is that it’s Real Madrid, and anything – however small – gets blown out of all proportion and takes on a completely crazy media dimension. “Something that wasn’t necessarily a problem ends up becoming one,” he said. The midfielder also explained how the incident prompted concern from people around him, while comparing the situation to tensions commonly seen in other sports. “Afterwards, everyone rang me to find out what was going on and if I was all right. “They want to know what happened, but these days you have to be very discreet. To reassure people, I had to tell them that nothing was wrong. Valverde and Tchouameni have moved on from the incident. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “I once saw an NFL documentary and these things happen there all the time.” Tchouameni and Valverde have moved on from the controversy The controversy attracted further attention after club president Florentino Pérez publicly played down the incident, arguing that disagreements between teammates were not unusual, although the fact that the episode became public was problematic. Tchouameni has now made clear that his relationship with Valverde remains intact, both inside the dressing room and on the pitch. “If you walk into the dressing room today, as Mourinho said, you’ll see that Valverde and I are fine; there’s no problem between us. “On the pitch, there’s no problem either – life goes on. And in fact, even these things bring you closer to the other person. We’re fine; we don’t have any problems,” he concluded.

item.title: Forest's start raises questions - but belief in Glasner remains
item.description: Nottingham Forest have lost five of their opening eight games in all competitions [Getty Images] "It feels unfair but I don't want to be complaining and feeling as victims." Oliver Glasner's words offer a positive outlook as he believes Nottingham Forest deserve more following their disappointing start to the season. They visit Ipswich Town on Friday following three straight defeats during an underwhelming opening which has left them in the Premier League's relegation zone. It was not a position they expected to be in after appointing Glasner in the summer, following his exit from Crystal Palace. They have been agonisingly close to successful results, wasting golden chances before losing at Palace and nearly hung on for a battling point against champions Arsenal last Sunday. There is also confidence internally Forest are still on the right track under Glasner, who has impressed with his methods and personality. item.content:encoded: Nottingham Forest have lost five of their opening eight games in all competitions [Getty Images] "It feels unfair but I don't want to be complaining and feeling as victims." Oliver Glasner's words offer a positive outlook as he believes Nottingham Forest deserve more following their disappointing start to the season. They visit Ipswich Town on Friday following three straight defeats during an underwhelming opening which has left them in the Premier League's relegation zone. It was not a position they expected to be in after appointing Glasner in the summer, following his exit from Crystal Palace. They have been agonisingly close to successful results, wasting golden chances before losing at Palace and nearly hung on for a battling point against champions Arsenal last Sunday. There is belief that progress is being made, but it needs to translate on the pitch. There is also confidence internally Forest are still on the right track under Glasner, who has impressed with his methods and personality. He was brought in to take Forest to the next level after lifting the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League with Palace. Glasner is impatient to repeat that success, detailing how owner Evangelos Marinakis is the only person he has met with more ambition than him. The 52-year-old has also said he is not a magician and has already spoken to Marinakis about previous slow starts. He won just one of his opening six games at Palace after replacing Roy Hodgson in February 2024 and then did not win any of his first eight games in his first full season with the Eagles in 2024-25. That campaign finished with Palace beating Manchester City in the FA Cup final to end a 119-year wait for a first major trophy. Glasner has reiterated the need for a strategy and consistency at Forest and it is just over a year since Ange Postecoglou's 39-day reign ended after six defeats and no wins in eight games. Sean Dyche lasted a little over 100 days and while Vitor Pereira took Forest to the Europa League semi-finals and achieved top-flight survival, he was sacked just two minutes before a termination clause expired in June. Glasner's consistency is starting to become clear with a preferred line-up crystalising with Neco Williams, Matz Sels, Dan Ndoye, Murillo and James McAtee starting every league game. Morgan Gibbs-White would have done so on Sunday too but for a muscle injury. Club captain Ryan Yates is yet to play a minute, Ibrahim Sangare has managed just one start - despite signing a new three-year contract in the summer - while Callum Hudson-Odoi has had his playing time limited and Ola Aina has lost his place to new wing-back Daniel Munoz. Given the results, certainly at home, some will be forgiven for believing they deserve more minutes and the players are aware of the growing expectation and pressure. "We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas," said defender Murillo following the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal. "We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best. "Now we are building our confidence, I think. We have a very good team, experienced players as well. Now we keep going because we know how tough the Premier League is." Lowest conversion rate in the league Forest are yet to score in the Premier League at the City Ground this season. They have netted just eight times in the league at home in 2026 so their struggles in front of their own fans are not new. They were masked by the Europa League victories against Ferencvaros, Porto and Aston Villa but, in the league, they have won just two of 17 home games since November. Of those eight goals, four were scored against a weak Burnley side in April and they have now gone eight hours and 26 minutes without netting at home. Overall this season, Forest have scored five times but have a -6.20 xG, which is the worst in the division. They have had the third-highest number of shots in the Premier League with 120, only behind Manchester United (138) and free-scoring Brighton (125), but only 25 have been on target. Against the Gunners, they had 14 shots but only two on target and Rory Delap's miss against Palace, Walter Benitez saving his close-range blast , summed up Forest's lack of cutting edge. It meant Forest have a conversion rate of just 4.17% - the lowest in the division after Spurs rose to 6.06% following Monday's win over Coventry. "Every team in the Premier League has the quality to come back into a game to score a goal," said Glasner. "When you play the champions, you don't have seven, eight or nine moments like we had at Palace. You have two or three or four, and if you don't take it, you have always the chance to lose the game." That view followed spending £50m on striker Delap this summer, who earned praise from Glasner against Arsenal and was also denied by Ezri Konsa's fine block in injury time. It is clear the intention is there and the Austrian has no desire to dwell on the past. "We are the only ones who can change it," he added. "I told the players this is a tough moment and in tough moments in life there's just one way to go through it, you need your family, you need your your friends and you need to stick together and stay positive "I'm very convinced that we will do this because I know the players and all the character of the players then we will get these scores, we will get the results."

item.title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
item.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found. (Image credit: Gregorio Borgia)

item.title: Bears’ Caleb Williams pours heart out to Cole Kmet after possibly serious knee injury
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears’ Caleb Williams pours heart out to Cole Kmet after possibly serious knee injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears secured a thrilling 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football, but the mood inside Soldier Field remained heavy after the final whistle. Veteran tight end Cole Kmet suffered a potentially serious knee injury during the contest, leaving his teammates and fanbase holding their breath. Kmet was carted off the field during the second half after collapsing in obvious pain, immediately drawing deep concern from players on both sidelines. Before his sudden departure, Kmet continued serving as a reliable target in Chicago’s passing attack. Quarterback Caleb Williams delivered a brilliant performance overall, completing 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns to guide Chicago to victory. However, those impressive numbers mattered very little to Williams after watching one of his closest offensive teammates go down. Speaking with reporters in the postgame locker room, an emotional Williams poured his heart out when asked about Kmet’s massive impact on his personal growth and the team’s culture. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Cole’s been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year,” Williams said. “I don’t have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team. I’ll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is.” Caleb Williams on Cole Kmet's Injury: "Cole's been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team. I'll be right there with him… pic.twitter.com/SVdqred2Kn — Bears on Real (@BearsOnReal) October 23, 2026 Kmet’s presence has proven vital to Williams’ rapid development under head coach Ben Johnson. Beyond his physical blocking and clutch receiving talent, the veteran tight end serves as an essential leader in the locker room and a trusted safety valve on key downs. Losing him for an extended period would deal a major blow to a surging offensive unit currently firing on all cylinders. While Chicago anxiously awaits official medical updates and imaging results on Kmet’s knee, Williams made it clear that the entire team will stand firmly beside their star playmaker throughout every step of his recovery process. Related: Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez can only tip his cap to Caleb Williams after loss to Bears Related: Bears’ Ben Johnson gives Drake Maye his flowers after electric TNF showdown

item.title: How 'The Purdue Way' reportedly defies college basketball roster spending
item.description: Because Purdue basketball prefers building its roster from within, it doesn't spend as much to lure players. In a new report from CBS Sports , the Boilermakers are in the sixth tier (of seven) of college basketball spending, between $7.1 million and $9.9 million for the 2026-27 season. That's the same tier as Butler , and far below Indiana , which is in the second tier at just under $20 million. CBS marvels at how Purdue gets quite a bang for its buck. "Get a load of this: Purdue has won 12 NCAA Tournament games over the last five years. The other 13 teams in this tier have combined for eight Big Dance wins in that same five-year window, with three of them coming from Iowa last March. (Coach) Matt Painter has used brutal honesty and a humming offense to create an environment that most players don't want to leave, even if there is more money elsewhere. "Purdue will take one graduate transfer to fill a specific void, but it doesn't mine the portal for multiple starters year after year. Finding hidden gems is the secret sauce. Painter saw that there was more than met the eye in Zach Edey and Braden Smith and developed them into All-American and/or National Player of the Year talents. The Purdue Way might be impossible to replicate. Marquette certainly tried to emulate the homegrown talent approach, but that turned sour in a hurry in 2025-26. Purdue still has not taken a single transfer who was not a graduate transfer in Painter's two-decade run leading the program. It's one of the wildest stats of the modern era of college basketball." CBS used more than 100 sources during several weeks of research to gauge college basketball roster spending for 79 power conference teams and Gonzaga. The average roster costs $13.5 million this season, up from about $7 million last season. These are based on every team's current roster and their players' maximum earnings potential. The average Big Ten school spends $12.7 million on its roster, lower than the SEC and the Big East, but more than the Big 12 and ACC. CBS notes that fifth-year players who are currently permitted to play count toward a team's total, so that could fluctuate. Also, player incentives could change a team's spending total at the end of the season. Purdue basketball roster 2026-27 (Number, name, height, year/previous school or nation) 0, C.J.
