item.title: Wolves loanee is fast becoming a fan favourite at Ajax after another crucial goal against Atalanta
item.description: Wolves loanee is fast becoming a fan favourite at Ajax after another crucial goal against Atalanta Tolu Arokodare was at it again for Ajax . The striker, on loan from Wolves, grabbed an 87th minute goal at home to Atalanta as Ajax grabbed an important victory in the Europa Conference League. Arokodare then turned provider, assisting Abdellah Ouazane who scored a fantastic goal. Arokodare may be listed as the assist provider for the goal, but it really was a solo effort from the Moroccan teenager. The victory means that Ajax have bounced back from an opening day defeat to Croatian side Hajduk Split. Atalanta were one of the favourites to win the competition and this victory for Ajax proves that they really should be thinking of the Conference League as a European competition they have a real chance of winning. For Arokodare, his loan spell from Wolves could not be going better. With eight goals and three assists in 13 games, he has surpassed his number from 38 games with Wolves last season. He is fast becoming a fan favourite at the Dutch club as his personality and goals are endearing him to a fanbase that is enjoying what they are seeing from the 25-year-old from Nigeria. Whether Ajax are willing to lift the purchase option they agreed with Wolves at the end of the season remains to be seen, but if Arokodare continues to score and enjoy the adoration of the fans, it will be hard for Ajax to not bring him in permanently next summer. Next up for Ajax and Arokodare is a trip to Rotterdam to face Sparta. After a 5-2 victory over FC Groningen in their last Eredivisie game, Ajax are in fourth place, five points behind Feyenoord in first. With PSV and Feyenoord playing each other this weekend, there is a chance for Ajax to reduce the gap to both sides with a victory on Sunday afternoon. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: “PSV can also surprise Real Madrid”: José Mourinho Warned About PSV After Dominant Win Over Porto
item.description: Portuguese media have warned José Mourinho not to underestimate PSV Eindhoven after Peter Bosz’s side produced an impressive performance to defeat FC Porto 1-0 in the Champions League , with one journalist suggesting the Dutch champions could even surprise Real Madrid. PSV controlled large portions of Tuesday’s contest at the Estádio do Dragão, with Guus Til scoring the decisive goal. Their aggressive pressing, intensity and ability to dictate the tempo left a strong impression in Portugal, where Porto struggled to impose themselves on home soil. The performance also caught the attention of Portuguese football observers familiar with PSV, with one club journalist drawing comparisons between the challenge Bosz’s team could pose to Porto and their upcoming European opponents. PSV had enough opportunities to take the lead against Porto before half-time, yet they went into the break at 0-0 [IMAGO/Pro Shots] Porto Players Knew What To Expect From PSV Several members of Francesco Farioli’s squad were already familiar with PSV’s playing style before the match. Pablo Rosario, Santiago Giménez and Inbeom Hwang had previous experience of facing the Eindhoven club, meaning the visitors’ aggressive approach should not have come as a complete surprise. Hwang acknowledged that Porto knew the quality PSV possessed, but admitted that his team had failed to make the most of their opportunities. “We all knew that they had a good team, especially Santiago Giménez and me, because we had already faced them several times in the Netherlands,” Hwang said after the match. “We also got chances, but we didn't score and they did. That's how it is in the Champions League. We still have five matches ahead of us. We'll go all out and I believe we can do much better.” Rosario had also reportedly shared information about PSV with his coach before the encounter. However, any familiarity with Bosz’s methods did little to prevent Porto from being dominated for long periods. The defeat was particularly frustrating for the home supporters. Porto’s players made a lap of honour after the final whistle, but sections of the crowd responded with boos rather than applause, underlining the disappointment surrounding the performance. PSV travel to face Real Madrid on 13 November [IMAGO/PS Images] Portuguese Journalist Sends Warning To Mourinho PSV’s display has now prompted a warning for Mourinho ahead of their upcoming Champions League meeting with Real Madrid . A Portuguese journalist who regularly follows Benfica, Sporting Lisbon and Porto was particularly impressed by the Dutch side’s ability to take control of a match away from home. “This was a very unpleasant experience for FC Porto. I have never experienced anything like this before, that an opponent is so dominant in its own stadium,” the journalist said. PSV is able to speed up the ball, is strong in the pressing, aggressive in winning the ball back, and physically on a par.” The journalist then delivered a clear message about the threat Bosz’s side could pose in Madrid. “This PSV can also surprise Real Madrid,” he added, as quoted by PSV Inside . The warning comes as PSV prepare for their remaining Champions League fixtures, with Club Brugge due to visit the Philips Stadion before the Dutch side travel to face Real Madrid on 13 November. PSV have demonstrated that they can take the initiative against experienced European opposition [IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire] Bosz’s Side Earning Respect Across Europe The Porto victory has strengthened the impression that PSV can compete with leading European opposition when their pressing and possession-based football work together effectively. Tommie van der Leegte also suggested after the match that PSV, performing at this level, could beat any opponent. The Portuguese journalist’s comments echo that confidence, particularly after Porto struggled to cope with the visitors’ intensity in their own stadium. For Mourinho, the assessment serves as a reminder that PSV should not be judged solely by their domestic standing or recent results. Bosz’s team have demonstrated that they can take the initiative against experienced European opposition. Their next Champions League assignments will provide a clearer indication of how far that performance can carry them. But after leaving Porto with three points and widespread praise, PSV have given their future opponents plenty to consider.

item.title: Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez can only tip his cap to Caleb Williams after loss to Bears
item.description: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez can only tip his cap to Caleb Williams after loss to Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots ran out of steam against the Chicago Bears on Thursday, absorbing a tough loss, 30-24, at Soldier Field. The Patriots had their three-game winning streak snapped and fell to 4-3. The Bears, on the other hand, improved to 5-2. Caleb Williams starred in his second game back from a hamstring injury. He went 22-of-33 for 308 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. He made all the right reads in crunch time, and Christian Gonzalez could not help but be in awe of the third-year quarterback. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Caleb is an amazing quarterback. That play to Rome (Odunze), the ball went maybe a millimeter above KB’s (Kevin Byard) finger. If it was a little bit lower, KB would have tipped it. Who knows what would have happened?” said Gonzalez in the video posted by Patriots Reports’ Zach Gatsby. “So that’s just one you tip your hat to. He made an amazing throw and a good catch (by Odunze). So, it’s the NFL. They’re going to make plays. We’re gonna make plays. It’s a battle to see who comes out on top.” 🚨Christian Gonzalez on Caleb Williams' game-winning plays: “Caleb is an amazing quarterback. You know, that play to Rome, I mean, the ball went maybe a millimeter above KB's finger. If it was a little bit lower, KB would have tipped it. And, I mean, who knows what would have… pic.twitter.com/IFfbKr0Cbe — Gatsby (@ZachGatsby) October 23, 2026 The 24-year-old Williams became the first quarterback in team history to record over 300 yards in consecutive games since Mitch Trubisky in 2018. Drake Maye was not too shabby, throwing 24-of-31 for 321 yards, two touchdowns, and one pick. He had four carries for 26 yards. His valiant effort, however, was not enough to outlast the Bears. Gonzalez logged four tackles. The Patriots stayed afloat after Andy Borregales kicked a 47-yard field goal with 37 seconds left. The Bears, however, recovered the ensuing onside kick. Related: Bears’ Ben Johnson gives Drake Maye his flowers after electric TNF showdown Related: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel takes the high road on Will Campbell’s controversial penalty in loss to Bears

item.title: Borussia Dortmund vs. Eintracht Frankfurt preview: A Topspiel to iron out issues
item.description: Borussia Dortmund vs. Eintracht Frankfurt preview: A Topspiel to iron out issues Borussia Dortmund Taking the headline slot on Matchday 7 of the Bundesliga this weekend, Borussia Dortmund welcome Eintracht Frankfurt to the Westfalenstadion this Saturday. As is normal, kick-off in the Topspiel affair is at 18:30 CET. Dortmund's form has been turbulent to say the least in recent weeks. Last Saturday's 0-0 stalemate with 1.FC Union Berlin sounded the alarm bells at the Westphalian club. Most notably, their lack of cutting edge in attack. Much to Niko Kovač's relief, the Champions League provided a chance to bounce back to winning ways. However it was far from smooth as Serhou Guirassy's brace downed minnows Sabah in an extremely wasteful performance. Kovač and Ole Book have now asked of their squad that they act "more ruthless" in front of goal. BVB ought to be confident too, seeing as they have extracted victory over Frankfurt in 9 of the last 10 games played on home soil. Team news: Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias (ACL tears) remain out, while BVB confirmed Kostas Karetsas (ligament injury) will sit out against Frankfurt. Justin Lerma (muscular problems) is another long-term absentee for now. Eintracht Frankfurt Adding an extra bit of spice to this encounter is the fact that Eintracht Frankfurt have also lacked consistency in the form chart. They also bid farewell to sporting director Markus Krösche, likely marking the start of a new era. Impressive wins over rivals Mainz 05 and 1.FC Köln have been high points, but heavy defeats against Augsburg and RB Leipzig exposed weaknesses. Instability in defence is a worry while a new-look midfield aim to find their feet. One thing that Adi Hütter could use in his favour is versatility. The 56-year-old has used both 4-4-2 and 3-4-2-1 systems this season to varying effects. Something that could come handy if they hope to stymie Dortmund's tempo. The biggest hurdle for Frankfurt this Saturday seems to be a mental one. The Hessen club have been more than a match for BVB at home, but they last tasted victory in front of the Yellow Wall all the way back in April 2021. Team news: Much to the relief of Adi Hütter, Frankfurt's injury list remains incredibly short. On Jessic Ngankam is sidelined with a hamstring injury. Meanwhile, Raphael Onyedika is at risk of a suspension with four yellow cards to his name.

item.title: Ducati says Aprilia “can do whatever they want” amid team order talks in MotoGP
item.description: Motorsport photo Ducati says it is not concerned by Aprilia potentially deploying team orders in the closing stages of the 2026 MotoGP season, saying its rival “can do whatever they want”. With just five rounds remaining in the season, the championship could swing in any direction, with Aprilia’s Jorge Martin holding a narrow two-point lead over Ducati star Marc Marquez . Given how high the stakes are, the possibility of team orders has been brought up repeatedly, particularly at Aprilia, which is chasing its maiden world title in the premier class. Ducati doesn’t appear to be in a position to instruct its riders to assist Marquez, with the 33-year-old enjoying a comfortable advantage over his team-mates on the Desmosedici. Already on Friday, the 33-year-old stated that “if you are fast, you don’t need team orders”, in what appeared to be a direct jibe at his title rival Martin, who was only third among the four Aprilias at the last round in Indonesia. Now Ducati itself has adopted a similar stance, saying its riders remain free to race against each other. “I would like to use what Marc said: ‘if you are fast, you don’t need help’. That’s it,” Ducati team manager Davide Tardozzi told MotoGP.com. Asked whether using team orders would take the shine off Aprilia’s success, Tardozzi replied: “They can do whatever they want. We are trying to focus only to be fast on track. “We know our opponents are very strong, but in the end, we are looking only to have the best results for Marc. And that’s it.” Watch: Marc Márquez on Retirement, Acosta and the Next King of MotoGP Aprilia explains stance After its dominant 1-2-3-4 result in Indonesia, Aprilia admitted for the first time that it is considering introducing team orders, but stopped short of specifying when it will take such action. On the eve of this weekend’s Australian Grand Prix, the Noale marque’s management sat down with its four riders at Phillip Island to reiterate its guidelines for the race. Aprilia has made it clear that it is still too early to use team orders, stressing that the focus is on ensuring its riders don’t collide with each other and give away points to rivals. However, with the margins so thin during the final year of the 1000cc cycle, Aprilia is aware that every single point could make a difference in the title fight. “The target is clear but we don’t want to say anything about rider orders,” Aprilia team manager Paolo Bonora told MotoGP.com. “We didn’t say [anything about] rider orders because we want to have all of the Aprilia guys in front. “We know that all of us together can do something very special. We didn’t say anything in Indonesia. “Yesterday, as usual, we had a meeting with all four riders, saying clearly that, as in the initial races, the clear word is respect, only respect. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Ducati says it is not concerned by Aprilia potentially deploying team orders in the closing stages of the 2026 MotoGP season, saying its rival “can do whatever they want”. With just five rounds remaining in the season, the championship could swing in any direction, with Aprilia’s Jorge Martin holding a narrow two-point lead over Ducati star Marc Marquez . Given how high the stakes are, the possibility of team orders has been brought up repeatedly, particularly at Aprilia, which is chasing its maiden world title in the premier class. Ducati doesn’t appear to be in a position to instruct its riders to assist Marquez, with the 33-year-old enjoying a comfortable advantage over his team-mates on the Desmosedici. Already on Friday, the 33-year-old stated that “if you are fast, you don’t need team orders”, in what appeared to be a direct jibe at his title rival Martin, who was only third among the four Aprilias at the last round in Indonesia. Now Ducati itself has adopted a similar stance, saying its riders remain free to race against each other. “I would like to use what Marc said: ‘if you are fast, you don’t need help’. That’s it,” Ducati team manager Davide Tardozzi told MotoGP.com. Asked whether using team orders would take the shine off Aprilia’s success, Tardozzi replied: “They can do whatever they want. We are trying to focus only to be fast on track. “We know our opponents are very strong, but in the end, we are looking only to have the best results for Marc. And that’s it.” Watch: Marc Márquez on Retirement, Acosta and the Next King of MotoGP Aprilia explains stance After its dominant 1-2-3-4 result in Indonesia, Aprilia admitted for the first time that it is considering introducing team orders, but stopped short of specifying when it will take such action. On the eve of this weekend’s Australian Grand Prix, the Noale marque’s management sat down with its four riders at Phillip Island to reiterate its guidelines for the race. Aprilia has made it clear that it is still too early to use team orders, stressing that the focus is on ensuring its riders don’t collide with each other and give away points to rivals. However, with the margins so thin during the final year of the 1000cc cycle, Aprilia is aware that every single point could make a difference in the title fight. “The target is clear but we don’t want to say anything about rider orders,” Aprilia team manager Paolo Bonora told MotoGP.com. “We didn’t say [anything about] rider orders because we want to have all of the Aprilia guys in front. “We know that all of us together can do something very special. We didn’t say anything in Indonesia. “Yesterday, as usual, we had a meeting with all four riders, saying clearly that, as in the initial races, the clear word is respect, only respect. Don’t take a risk with the same-bike riders. “If you have to overtake somebody, take care that it’s in a safe space. But everyone has the potential. And if Trackhouse would like to win, they would like to win as well as us. But we give them the possibility to do so because we know all four riders can achieve something special. “During that meeting, we were very clear: no orders at the moment. There is no reason at the moment to prevent ‘you’ from winning. But the only clear message is, as we told you after the fourth round, have respect for your team-mate and your Trackhouse mates as well because all together we can do something good and no risk.” Pressed further on when such team orders could be introduced, Bonora didn’t provide a specific deadline. “At the moment, we haven’t defined anything regarding this,” he said. “But it’s the first time we can achieve something very special, and it will not be very smart if we have something clear, so one point, two points, five points’ difference, and there is the possibility, why not? “But at the moment, no clear rider orders.” Read Also: MotoGP Australian GP: Marco Bezzecchi leads Aprilia 1-2-4-5 in Friday Practice Marc Marquez puts his chances of retiring within three years at 70% To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Revisiting Arch Manning's disaster 2023 recruiting class filled with 5-star QB flops
item.description: Revisiting Arch Manning's disaster 2023 recruiting class filled with 5-star QB flops originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas quarterback Arch Manning's 2026 season has been a disappointment so far. Despite high expectations in his second year as the Longhorns' starter, he has been subpar so far across his first six games. While there are several theories as to why Manning has struggled, the quarterback is far from the only five-star signal-caller from the class of 2023 recruiting class that has struggled. The class included fellow five-star quarterbacks including Dante Moore, Nico Iamaleava, Jackson Arnold and others. Let's take a look back at the class to see just how much the signal-callers failed to live up to expectations in college. MORE: Meet Arch Manning's entire family 2023 High School football recruiting class The 2023 high school recruiting class may be a thing of the past, but it has produced some big-time college and recent NFL draft picks. But when it comes to quarterbacks, the class hasn't exactly panned out, especially with the five-star guys. 5-star quarterbacks in 2023 Rankings from the 247Sports Composite were used. QB High School QB Ranking National Ranking School Arch Manning Isidore Newman No. 1 No. 1 Texas Nico Iamaleava Warren No. 2 No. 3 Tennessee Dante Moore Martin Luther King No. 3 No. 5 UCLA Jackson Arnold Denton Guyer No. 4 No. 8 Oklahoma Malachi Nelson Los Alamitos No. 5 No. 12 USC Arch Manning Manning has had a full season and a half as Texas' full-time starter, but he has yet to play consistently well in Austin so far. He opened the 2025 season with three interceptions thrown in his first three games, including in the Week 1 loss to Ohio State. He finished the season having thrown for 3,163 yards with 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions, rushing for another 399 yards and 10 touchdowns. But the Longhorns lost three games to OSU, Florida and Georgia that kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Manning had turnovers in all three of those losses. Manning's best season in 2026 came against Ohio State in Week 2. After struggling for three quarters, he led three touchdown drives in the fourth quarter in a thrilling come-from-behind 24-23 victory. His turnover issues have continued, however. He threw two interceptions during Texas' 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, including a pick-six. A week later, his strip-sack fumble sealed a Florida upset victory. As a result, Manning's backup KJ Lacey is seeing an up-tick in first-team reps ahead of Texas' game against No. 7 Ole Miss. "Looking back on Manning, I think we probably overvalued the between the ears stuff a little bit," 247Sports' Director of Scouting, Andrew Ivins, told The Sporting News via email. "I think everyone did. I mean he’s from football royalty. It was easy to assume that his superpower would be his ability to out-think defenses from the pocket – to anticipate and react at a different speed.

Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas quarterback Arch Manning's 2026 season has been a disappointment so far. Despite high expectations in his second year as the Longhorns' starter, he has been subpar so far across his first six games. While there are several theories as to why Manning has struggled, the quarterback is far from the only five-star signal-caller from the class of 2023 recruiting class that has struggled. The class included fellow five-star quarterbacks including Dante Moore, Nico Iamaleava, Jackson Arnold and others. MORE: Meet Arch Manning's entire family 2023 High School football recruiting class The 2023 high school recruiting class may be a thing of the past, but it has produced some big-time college and recent NFL draft picks. But when it comes to quarterbacks, the class hasn't exactly panned out, especially with the five-star guys. 5-star quarterbacks in 2023 Rankings from the 247Sports Composite were used. QB High School QB Ranking National Ranking School Arch Manning Isidore Newman No. 1 No. 1 Texas Nico Iamaleava Warren No. 2 No. 3 Tennessee Dante Moore Martin Luther King No. 3 No. 5 UCLA Jackson Arnold Denton Guyer No. 4 No. 8 Oklahoma Malachi Nelson Los Alamitos No. 5 No. 12 USC Arch Manning Manning has had a full season and a half as Texas' full-time starter, but he has yet to play consistently well in Austin so far. He opened the 2025 season with three interceptions thrown in his first three games, including in the Week 1 loss to Ohio State. He finished the season having thrown for 3,163 yards with 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions, rushing for another 399 yards and 10 touchdowns. But the Longhorns lost three games to OSU, Florida and Georgia that kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Manning had turnovers in all three of those losses. Manning's best season in 2026 came against Ohio State in Week 2. After struggling for three quarters, he led three touchdown drives in the fourth quarter in a thrilling come-from-behind 24-23 victory. His turnover issues have continued, however. He threw two interceptions during Texas' 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, including a pick-six. A week later, his strip-sack fumble sealed a Florida upset victory. As a result, Manning's backup KJ Lacey is seeing an up-tick in first-team reps ahead of Texas' game against No. 7 Ole Miss. "Looking back on Manning, I think we probably overvalued the between the ears stuff a little bit," 247Sports' Director of Scouting, Andrew Ivins, told The Sporting News via email. "I think everyone did. I mean he’s from football royalty. It was easy to assume that his superpower would be his ability to out-think defenses from the pocket – to anticipate and react at a different speed. That hasn’t really materialized. Is that on Manning? I don’t know. We always talk about the three Ps when it comes to quarterbacks. Protection. Playmakers. Playcallers. Texas has two potential Day 1 picks at offensive tackle. They outbid plenty this offseason for Cam Coleman. But nothing ever looks easy in that offense." Nico Iamaleava Iamaleava started at Tennessee as a backup to Joe Milton in 2023, but earned the nod as a starter in 2024. That year, he helped lead Tennessee to its first-ever CFP berth. While the Vols relied on a successful ground game on offense, Iamaleave played well enough. He threw for 2,616 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions while rushing for 358 yards and three scores. He surprisingly transferred to UCLA in April 2025 after a messy exit from Tennessee stemming from an alleged NIL contract dispute. He was the Bruins' starter in 2025, as UCLA limped to a 3-8 finish and fired head coach Deshaun Foster early in the year. He threw for a season-low 1,928 yards with 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions, but had 505 rush yards and three touchdowns. "Iamaleava led Tennessee to the College Football Playoff and was on track to do the same thing at UCLA before his injury," Ivins added. "Is he a complete product? No. But he entered the season with a second-round grade from Sunday evaluators. I think that would surprise a lot of people." Although there were rumors that Iamaleava may transfer in the wake of the Foster firing, he remained at UCLA as new head coach Bob Chesney joined the fold. He got the Bruins off to a 5-0 start, but suffered a season-ending torn ACL injury in the first half of the Ducks' 17-15 win over Nebraska, cutting his season short. He had thrown two interceptions in the first half of that game, as well. Dante Moore Moore's recruitment to UCLA was interesting, as he was a longtime commitment to Dan Lanning's staff at Oregon before flipping to the Bruins late. His true freshman season in Los Angeles was a roller-coaster, as he got the Bruins out to a 4-2 start in mid-October. But he started to see less playing time after throwing six interceptions in three games against Utah, Washington State and Oregon State. He played in just three games the rest of the season for UCLA, and entered the portal in late November, and committed, as expected, to Oregon. He served as the backup to Dillon Gabriel in 2024. As a starter for the Ducks last season, he had the best season of his career, throwing for 3,565 yards with 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Oregon went 11-1 in the regular season, losing to eventual national champion Indiana. The Ducks defeated James Madison 51-34 in the first round, and dismantled Texas Tech 23-0 in the Orange Bowl. Oregon fell 56-22 to Indiana in the Peach Bowl semifinal, as Moore threw four interceptions in his last three games. As Oregon's starter this season, he led the Ducks to a 3-1 start before leaving the game with a concussion against USC on Sept. 26. He hasn't been cleared to play since. Jackson Arnold Arnold has had a journeyman of a career so far. He started his career at Oklahoma, where he was Dillon Gabriel's primary backup in 2023. He earned the starting role at Oklahoma in 2024, and the Sooners started 3-0. But after throwing an interception against Tennessee in Week 4, he was benched in favor of backup Michael Hawkins Jr. He did not see playing time in the next two games against Auburn and Texas. But Oklahoma went back to Arnold as the starter for the Sooners' final six games of the season. He finished 2-4 across those games, and threw for 1,421 yards with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions, taking 34 sacks on the year. He transferred to Auburn ahead of the 2025 season, where he was once again benched after the Tigers' four-game losing streak from Sept. 20-Oct. 18. He did not see much playing time the rest of the season. Perhaps the third time is the charm for Arnold, as he has since transferred to UNLV. He's had his best statistical season so far, throwing for 1,386 yards with 10 touchdowns and two interceptions with 408 rush yards and six touchdowns. The Rebels are 4-3 on the season. Malachi Nelson Perhaps the quietest of all the former five-star signal-callers is Malachi Nelson. Since being named Caleb Williams backup at USC in 2023, he failed to win the starting job at his next stop at Boise State, and played in just six games at UTEP last season. He is now at Syracuse, where he earned starts due to injury in games against Virginia and Louisville. The Orange lost both games, and Nelson is now dealing with injuries of his own. Across his four teams, he's thrown for 1,823 yards with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. "It’s not easy scouting quarterbacks," Ivins said of the 5-stars from 2023 that fell off. "It’s also not easy to develop them. Both Manning and Iamaleva were at the top of the board for us because they have legitimate NFL traits – things that few individuals possess. And when ever

item.title: Today’s Papers: Woltemade steps up, Maignan costs Milan, Atalanta in crisis
item.description: Today’s Papers: Woltemade steps up, Maignan costs Milan, Atalanta in crisis La Gazzetta dello Sport Milan sunk What a thrashing in Bournemouth, cups fading away Maignan sent off, penalty doubt, the Diavolo down collapse with 10 men and lose 3-0, now in 24th place. McKennie hits the post. Overtaken by Dia via a penalty. The German equalises from the spot as well. Lucumi scores in the 89th, but is offside. Carnevali: ‘The hotseat is always hot at this club’ Como, the cup of Champions Paz and Douvikas up in the big leagues (including Yamal) Inter Carlos Augusto signs a contract renewal after his goals Corriere dello Sport Juve all heart Rennes comeback: Woltemade steps up VAR heartbreak at the end | a reaction after the flop against Lazio: 2-2 in the Europa League Celik opens the scoring, Al-Taamari responds. McKennie hits the post. Overtaken by Dia via a penalty. The German equalises from the spot as well. Lucumi scores in the 89th, but is offside. Spalletti seventh: 7 points in three games Maignan causes damage Milan down to 1- men: Lose 3-0 in Bournemouth Kluivert opens the scoring, Mike brings down Adams in the area: Red card in the 28th minute and another a penalty. Tavernier scores past Torriani, then the goal from Adli arrives Ajax sink Sarri Atalanta in crisis: 2-0 The Carlos Augusto dance A starting sport and a contract renewal: Four goals in seven games DeLa: ‘I’m not selling to an American’ ‘I’d always prefer to sell the club to a Neopolitan’ Pellegrini scares Gasp High-grade tear in his thigh, Dybala speeds up Suwarso, Como’s needle Fabregas, the four goals against United and a dream that was born in Serie D Tuttosport Wolte e basta Juve 2-2 Rennes More disappointment, more boos and more fear for Spalletti: Only the German shows the right spirit Woltemade sets up Celik for 1-0 and scores the equalising goal for 2-2 from the penalty spot, he tries all the time and plays for his teammates. However, the confusion and errors from the Bianconeri are baffling. They were punished by Al-Taamari and Dia, who scored from the spot. A goal for 3-2 from Lucumi was disallowed for a questionable offside call. Carnevali: ‘The hotseat is getting hotter, but you can’t change every time. Spalletti knows what he needs to do’. The coach attacks the referee and lashes out at the talk of his sacking: ‘I will continue to not sleep at night’ Maignan madness costs Milan 3-0 against Bournemouth with two penalties, the goalkeeper shoves Adams in the face and is sent off: Rossoneri down to 10 for over an hour at the mercy of the English. The second European defeat is costly ‘Toro, you’ve found soul, now lets win with venom’ Against Monza at 19.45: Abate always wants more The coach is asking for his third consecutive win: ‘A re-match of the cup match against Juric? No. On his discussions with Vlasic: ‘Play without cares and you will unlock yourself, like Simeone’ Atalanta collapse, Sarri teetering Conference League: Ajax win 2-0 at the end

item.title: 'We did not play on our highest level' - Fabian Hurzeler rues missed chances as Brighton held to shock draw away at Jablonec
item.description: Head coach Fabian Hurzeler was left frustrated by poor finishing after Brighton were held to a surprise goalless Conference League draw away against Jablonec. The disappointing stalemate in the Czech Republic brought an abrupt end to the impressive six-match winning streak the Premier League outfit had built up across all competitions this season. German tactician laments wasteful display Hurzeler admitted his heavily rotated side fell below their usual standards after failing to mark his 100th match in charge with victory in the Czech Republic. Having plundered 22 goals across six straight wins, the Seagulls made wholesale changes following Sunday's 5-0 Premier League rout of Crystal Palace . Georginio Rutter squandered two first-half openings after netting a brace in their previous European outing, before Malick Yalcouye's 50th-minute effort was ruled offside. Stubborn hosts frustrate dominant visitors imago-sport-1084887708.jpg Despite the visitors failing to find a breakthrough, goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen still had to make late stops to deny Jiri Slama and Vakhtang Tchanturishvili on the break to preserve a fifth consecutive clean sheet in all competitions. Speaking to TNT Sports after the final whistle, Hurzeler insisted his players must execute the fundamentals much better in European competition: "We did not play on our highest level; Jablonec defended well and defended the box well, good movement in transition. Overall, not the result we wanted, but we have to keep going. "If you play 0-0, then you didn't create enough; that's definitely something we have to get better at. We have to understand what it needs to play in this Cup. Understand we have to be brilliant at the basics. We weren't good at the basics; that's something we have to improve." Wayward finishing undermines statistical control The Premier League side dominated the contest statistically, recording 72.1 per cent possession, 63 final-third entries and 56 touches inside the opposition penalty area. However, they tested the home keeper just four times from 26 total shots, generating a modest tally of 1.42 expected goals against a disciplined defensive block. Asked to explain why his forwards struggled to carve out clear-cut opportunities despite such territorial dominance, Hurzeler added: "Good defending and crosses not where we wanted to have them. The precision in the last action was missing; that's something we have to improve. "The longer the game got, the more space they had to make transitions. We tried to push hard for scoring the goal, and of course they had the space to make countermovements. In certain moments, we were lucky. "We always learn. I think it's important to take things away from this game and improve in the next game. There is no time for a lot of disappointment; we have to focus on the next game." Recalling his rested regular starters should give the Seagulls a much sharper edge in the final third on Merseyside.

item.title: 5 'Solo Leveling' Characters Who Deserved So Much Better
item.description: Jin-woo starts out as a weak E-Rank hunter trapped in a seemingly endless struggle to survive. Before long, though, he becomes an unstoppable force. His progression feels steady and earned, and his efforts to uncover the source of his abilities take him through a series of unforgettable fights.

item.title: Juventus drops first European points after late drama
item.description: Juventus drops first European points after late drama Juventus and Rennes played out a 2-2 draw in the Europa League last night after a potential late winner for the Bianconeri was ruled out following a VAR check. Juventus welcomed Rennes to the Allianz Stadium days after suffering a shock 3-0 defeat to Lazio at home in Serie A over the weekend. The result had left supporters hoping for a much improved performance from their team in Europe. Luciano Spalletti was not banned from the touchline this time, giving him the opportunity to guide his players throughout the match. However, as has been the case in several recent games, Rennes proved the stronger side during the first half. Juventus took the lead through Zeki Celik just after five minutes, but Rennes gradually gained control of the contest. The Ligue 1 side soon found an equaliser through Mousa Tamari before Boulaye Dia converted a penalty just before half-time to put the visitors ahead. Juventus respond after the break Spalletti needed to deliver the right message to his players during the interval, with Juventus facing the prospect of another disappointing result. The Bianconeri returned for the second half with greater determination, and their performance improved considerably. The home side began to apply more pressure and looked more threatening going forward. Their efforts eventually paid off when Nick Woltemade converted a penalty to make it 2-2, bringing Juventus back into the contest and giving the supporters renewed hope of a positive result. The equaliser also changed the atmosphere inside the Allianz Stadium, as Juventus continued to search for a decisive goal. Having struggled to impose themselves before the break, Juve showed greater urgency and purpose in the second half. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) VAR denies Juventus a late winner Juventus appeared to have completed their comeback late in the match when Jhon Lucumi believed he had scored the winning goal. However, the celebrations were cut short after the referee reviewed the incident with the assistance of VAR. Following the check, the goal was ruled out, denying the Bianconeri a dramatic victory in front of their home supporters. Juventus were consequently forced to settle for a 2-2 draw despite their improved second-half display. Although the result offered Juventus a point, the match highlighted their inconsistency across the two halves. After falling behind against a determined Rennes side, they fought back impressively, only to see their hopes of a late winner disappear following the VAR intervention.

item.title: Nico Paz: Man United and Chelsea eye Como star as Real Madrid hold transfer advantage
item.description: Nico Paz: Man United and Chelsea eye Como star as Real Madrid hold transfer advantage Manchester United’s poor season took another dismal turn in midweek when they were ripped apart by Como in the Champions League. Michael Carrick’s team conceded in the second minute of the game and went on to lose the tie 4-1. It was the Red Devils’ second consecutive defeat in the European competition this season. The English giants also lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the previous tie. To put things into perspective, United have now lost five of their 11 games in all competitions this season, winning just two. They are 13th in the Premier League table after seven games and have already exited the EFL Cup. The Red Devils have struggled to impress in the final third, with Bruno Fernandes suffering a prolonged dip in form. The situation has prompted the English giants to draw up succession plans, and they appear to have found an option in Serie A. United eyeing Nico Paz According to Spanish newspaper AS, as cited by Tuttomercatoweb , United and Chelsea both have their eyes on Como’s Nico Paz. The Argentine arrived at Como from Real Madrid in the summer of 2024 and has developed in leaps and bounds since. Last season, the 22-year-old registered 13 goals and eight assists in 40 appearances across competitions. His efforts helped the Italian club finish fourth in the league and secure qualification for the Champions League. This campaign, Paz has already shifted up a gear, registering four goals and five assists in 10 games across all competitions. Nico Paz Stats: 2026/27 Season Source: Transfermarkt . His efforts appear to have earned him admirers at Old Trafford, especially after a blockbuster display in midweek. The Argentine tormented United, scoring two goals and setting up one more. Real Madrid have buy-back clause The report goes on to confirm that Real Madrid have a buy-back clause in Paz’s contract that can be exercised next summer. It states: “Real Madrid, however, have a buy-back clause (€80 million) which is only valid next summer, from 1 to 15 July.” The Serie A side, however, are keen to build a team around the Argentine, with the report adding: “As for Como, on the other hand, the intention and hope is to keep him, the darling of the Como fans, to build an ever-stronger team.” Paz is under contract until 2028, but given his incredible recent rise, the player could spark a bidding war for his signature next summer. Final Thoughts Paz could be a fine long-term replacement for Fernandes at Old Trafford. However, United must get their act together on the pitch if they wish to attract top talents like the Argentine in 2027. item.title: Dennis Tueart: City’s Man for all Seasons | Tueart 50
item.description: Dennis Tueart: City’s Man for all Seasons | Tueart 50 (COPY) How Dave Watson cemented his place in City and England folklore By Neil Leigh October 5 saw former City and England central defender Dave Watson, one of the totems of City’s famous 1976 League Cup winning side, celebrate his landmark 80th birthday. A veritable warrior and colossus on the field, Watson literally shed blood, sweat and tears across four special years at Maine Road – a period capped that by famous day at Wembley in February 1976 where his herculean efforts helped City beat Newcastle United 2-1. However, his impact and influence went far, far beyond that. Over the course of a hugely illustrious and successful playing career that spanned three decades in total, Watson – or The Rock as he was affectionately known - became synonymous for being one of the most talented and bravest English centre halves to play the game. Before joining City in 1975, Watson had already helped Sunderland, then of the old second division, beat Leeds United to win the 1973 FA Cup final, a result that still reverberates today as arguably the biggest shock in the competition’s history. That presaged a move to City where Big Dave was to arguably enjoy the greatest years of his career. Along the way Watson also became the backbone of the England national side – going on to win 65 caps in total and featuring for his country at the 1980 European Championships as well captaining the Three Lions on a number of occasions. In the wake of his landmark birthday, to mark Dave’s huge contribution to City, we gauged the thoughts and memories of Joe Corrigan, Peter Barnes, Dennis Tueart and Paul Power - four of his closest team-mates from both the Maine Road and England dressing rooms. For a man rightly revered as one of England’s great centre halves, the irony is that across the formative years of his career, Dave Watson was actually deployed as a centre forward! Hailing from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, Dave began his professional career as a striker with hometown club Notts County before then making the move to Rotherham United where he was to spend four seasons again playing upfront. It wasn’t until he joined Sunderland at the end of 1970 that the career – and position - for which he was to become so revered properly took full flight. For the first couple of years at Roker Park, Watson would again be largely deployed upfront – before the appointment of legendary manager Bob Stokoe revolutionised both his and Sunderland’s fortunes. The canny Stokoe recognised that Dave possessed all the necessary attributes – both physical and mental - to be a top-class centre half. The tactical switch proved a masterstroke from the get-go. Watson emerged as an inspirational figures, becoming joint top scorer across the Black Cats’ unforgettable passage to Wembley, as Sunderland entranced the nation by making their way to the 1973 FA Cup final. item.content:encoded: Dennis Tueart: City’s Man for all Seasons | Tueart 50 (COPY) How Dave Watson cemented his place in City and England folklore By Neil Leigh October 5 saw former City and England central defender Dave Watson, one of the totems of City’s famous 1976 League Cup winning side, celebrate his landmark 80th birthday. A veritable warrior and colossus on the field, Watson literally shed blood, sweat and tears across four special years at Maine Road – a period capped that by famous day at Wembley in February 1976 where his herculean efforts helped City beat Newcastle United 2-1. However, his impact and influence went far, far beyond that. Over the course of a hugely illustrious and successful playing career that spanned three decades in total, Watson – or The Rock as he was affectionately known - became synonymous for being one of the most talented and bravest English centre halves to play the game. Before joining City in 1975, Watson had already helped Sunderland, then of the old second division, beat Leeds United to win the 1973 FA Cup final, a result that still reverberates today as arguably the biggest shock in the competition’s history. That presaged a move to City where Big Dave was to arguably enjoy the greatest years of his career. Along the way Watson also became the backbone of the England national side – going on to win 65 caps in total and featuring for his country at the 1980 European Championships as well captaining the Three Lions on a number of occasions. In the wake of his landmark birthday, to mark Dave’s huge contribution to City, we gauged the thoughts and memories of Joe Corrigan, Peter Barnes, Dennis Tueart and Paul Power - four of his closest team-mates from both the Maine Road and England dressing rooms. For a man rightly revered as one of England’s great centre halves, the irony is that across the formative years of his career, Dave Watson was actually deployed as a centre forward! Hailing from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, Dave began his professional career as a striker with hometown club Notts County before then making the move to Rotherham United where he was to spend four seasons again playing upfront. It wasn’t until he joined Sunderland at the end of 1970 that the career – and position - for which he was to become so revered properly took full flight. For the first couple of years at Roker Park, Watson would again be largely deployed upfront – before the appointment of legendary manager Bob Stokoe revolutionised both his and Sunderland’s fortunes. The canny Stokoe recognised that Dave possessed all the necessary attributes – both physical and mental - to be a top-class centre half. The tactical switch proved a masterstroke from the get-go. Watson emerged as an inspirational figures, becoming joint top scorer across the Black Cats’ unforgettable passage to Wembley, as Sunderland entranced the nation by making their way to the 1973 FA Cup final. There they were pitted against Don Revie’s mighty Leeds United, the then pre-eminent force in the English footballing firmament. For many it looked a total mis-match. Instead, Watson and Co conjured up one of the greatest shocks in FA Cup history, Ian Porterfield’s famous goal securing a 1-0 win with Watson imperious in keeping Leeds’ famed strike force at bay. Not surprisingly those heroics helped bring his talent and temperament to the attention of a number of suitors, amongst them City – and so it was that Watson duly made the move to Maine Road in the summer of 1975 for a fee of £175,000. It was to prove one of the shrewdest ever investments by the Blues. His arrival into the big time had come relatively late. By then Watson was almost 29 – but like a fine wine, he was to prove one of those special and enduring vintages who simply got better and better with age, experience and maturity. In terms of the exciting, emerging City team being assembled by Tony Book, Watson was one of the defining final pieces in the jigsaw and instantly commanded both the respect and enduring admiration of his new team-mates. Amongst them was iconic City and England goalkeeper Joe Corrigan who was to become a close colleague and friend of Dave’s for both club and country as well as away from the pitch. Corrigan knows more than a thing or two about what makes a truly great defender. Over the course of an illustrious City career that spanned three decades, Joe played behind a host of outstanding centre backs. But for him Watson’s place in the City pantheon of elite centre backs is assured. “For me, Dave Watson is one of the best central defenders I ever played behind, and he epitomised the old-fashioned type of centre half,” Joe says today. “He was a fantastic player and a great header of the football. He scored one of the best headers I've ever seen against Ipswich in a league game in front of the North Stand at Maine Road. “It was just a bullet header from a Peter Barnes corner, but Dave just rose and smashed it in and it didn't even loop. It just went like an arrow straight into the top corner, back across the goal. Such a great goal. “He was always reliable, and such a great lad in the dressing room too and a wonderful professional. He may not have been the quickest, but he was such a great reader of the game. “If you could read the game, you were always in a position where you could deal with speed. So, for me he stands as one of the best centre-halves I've ever played with.” Though not the tallest by the traditional standards of English centre-halves at just around 6ft, Watson’s commanding presence, authority and no-nonsense attitude made him a force to be reckoned with. And for a young Peter Barnes, Watson’s natural fitness and physique was quite the sight to behold. “Dave was just a Colossus. I’d say he was like the Charles Bronson when he was getting changed into his City kit!,” Peter chuckles today. “His body was unbelievable. And to be on the field with him, Dave was one of those rare players who was so strong and powerful and such a force in the air. “I think if I had been an opposition player I’d have been terrified coming up against Dave.” That observation is amplified by another of the key members of the City dressing room across that era – Paul Power, a man who went on to skipper the Blues with huge distinction later in his career. “Dave was an unbelievable physical specimen,” Power declares. “I think if he hadn't been a footballer, he'd have probably been cast in some Western film. His physique was unbelievable. “In fact, I used to hide when we went in the shower. I let him go in one area then I'd get in another one round the corner!” For a young Peter Barnes meanwhile, navigating his way through the testing waters of top-flight professional football in the mid-1970s, the guidance, care and oversight afforded him by Watson is something he has never forgotten to this day. He credits Dave with being one of the key pillars of all that great City team assembled by Tony Book went on to achieve. Barnes also got to know The Rock well not just on the club front – but as cherished England colleagues too. And he says there was always much more to Watson the man than many would have suspected at first glance. A case in point being the former City winger’s memorable introduction to another of Dave’s private passions – his love for British rock legends Status Quo – back during Quo’s 1970s heyday. “Dave was and is such a lovely, lovely man and totally at odds off the field with how he was perceived as this tough defender,” Barnes says looking back. “He was like a gentle giant and had a lovely way with him. When he was in your company, he had a little bit of wit and mischief about him, and you know he'd done it all. “I remember one great occasion when I had an injury on my right knee just after I had broken into the team. Dave also had some trouble with his back at the time so it was arranged we would go to see a specialist in Slough. “It was a crucial time for me

item.title: United-States : Backlash over controversial Ohio midterms campaign ad
item.description: The backlash over an Ohio campaign advertisement attacking Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee for governor, spread beyond the state's borders Thursday, causing fresh headaches for Republicans with less than two weeks until the midterm elections.

item.title: Bears’ Ben Johnson gives Drake Maye his flowers after electric TNF showdown
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Bears’ Ben Johnson gives Drake Maye his flowers after electric TNF showdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson is helping incredibly talented quarterback Caleb Williams inch closer toward his potential after another terrific showing this season, as the NFC North squad outlasted the New Patriots for a 30-24 Thursday Night Football victory. The respected offensive mind commended No. 18 for a successful effort, but when given the opportunity by the media, he also extended praise to the opposing QB . Despite coming up short and tossing another back-breaking end-zone interception , Drake Maye demonstrated why he is already considered one of the best at his position. Johnson took notice. “He’s an outstanding player,” the 2025 Coach of the Year finalist said, per beat writer Zach Gatsby. “It’s very hard to bottle him up. You know, you only rush four, and he finds a way if he doesn’t see anything down the field to find an open gap and, you know, skirt on through. And then I think what’s really impressive is how he can find these little outlets and these dumps where they’re still running vertical for catch-and-run opportunities. item.title: Honesdale boys soccer battles West Scranton to a draw on senior night
item.description: HONESDALE — Emotions were running high Wednesday, Oct. 21, at the Daniel J. O’Neill Sports Complex as the Honesdale boys soccer team hosted West Scranton in a crucial late-season Lackawanna League showdown. It was Senior Night, and local fans had come out in force to honor six talented athletes who’ve meant a great deal to the program over the course of the past four years. Eli Carmody, Logan Lester, Karter Mikulak, Calvin Rosas, Carter Schweighofer and Aiden Tasker were feted in a moving ceremony prior to the match — one that left rookie head coach Mike Rosar feeling grateful. More: Valerio, Reed and Razny power Honesdale girls soccer to key league win Also by Kevin Edwards: Western Wayne girls soccer team cruises to big senior night victory “I am so thankful for this group of seniors,” Rosar said. “I hope these young men will look back fondly, not only on what they gained from their time with the program and the brotherhood they forged, but also on what they contributed and the foundation they've helped lay for the future.” And with those seniors leading the charge, Honesdale battled its way to a hard-fought 2-2 tie. The Hornets closed out their regular season with an overall record of 6-10-2. Next up is a berth in the District 2 playoffs, which begin Tuesday, Oct. 27 and run through Nov. 5. A grueling, physical battle Honesdale and West Scranton battled back and forth through the early portion of this Lackawanna League contest. But the Hornets struck first thanks to an electrifying play that brought the hometown fans to their feet. Karter Mikulak rocketed down the right wing on a deep ball that Invaders keeper Bryce McMillan pursued out of the box. Mikulak got there first by an eyelash and unleashed a textbook cross to Logan Lester, who deftly redirected it. Ethan Powers gathered in the ball and calmly buried it in the back of an empty net. The goal came at the 17:27 mark and gave Honesdale a 1-0 lead. That advantage lasted until West Scranton’s Kellan Burnside evened things up. The senior striker tallied an unassisted goal with 4:21 left in the half, sending the game to intermission with a 1-1 score. The Invaders surged into the lead less than five minutes into the second half as Maycol Gomez-Reyes notched an unassisted goal to put the visitors up 2-1. A grueling, physical slugfest ensued for the rest of the match with both teams receiving yellow cards along the way. Finally, as time ticked down in regulation, Honesdale broke through. Jase Berkihiser did the honors. The young midfielder converted a direct kick with 5:56 remaining in regulation, curling the ball beautifully into the upper right corner of the net and setting off a celebration in the stands. Berkihiser is just a sophomore, and it marked the first goal of his varsity career. item.content:encoded: HONESDALE — Emotions were running high Wednesday, Oct. 21, at the Daniel J. O’Neill Sports Complex as the Honesdale boys soccer team hosted West Scranton in a crucial late-season Lackawanna League showdown. It was Senior Night, and local fans had come out in force to honor six talented athletes who’ve meant a great deal to the program over the course of the past four years. Eli Carmody, Logan Lester, Karter Mikulak, Calvin Rosas, Carter Schweighofer and Aiden Tasker were feted in a moving ceremony prior to the match — one that left rookie head coach Mike Rosar feeling grateful. More: Valerio, Reed and Razny power Honesdale girls soccer to key league win Also by Kevin Edwards: Western Wayne girls soccer team cruises to big senior night victory “I am so thankful for this group of seniors,” Rosar said. “I hope these young men will look back fondly, not only on what they gained from their time with the program and the brotherhood they forged, but also on what they contributed and the foundation they've helped lay for the future.” And with those seniors leading the charge, Honesdale battled its way to a hard-fought 2-2 tie. The Hornets closed out their regular season with an overall record of 6-10-2. Next up is a berth in the District 2 playoffs, which begin Tuesday, Oct. 27 and run through Nov. 5. A grueling, physical battle Honesdale and West Scranton battled back and forth through the early portion of this Lackawanna League contest. But the Hornets struck first thanks to an electrifying play that brought the hometown fans to their feet. Karter Mikulak rocketed down the right wing on a deep ball that Invaders keeper Bryce McMillan pursued out of the box. Mikulak got there first by an eyelash and unleashed a textbook cross to Logan Lester, who deftly redirected it. Ethan Powers gathered in the ball and calmly buried it in the back of an empty net. The goal came at the 17:27 mark and gave Honesdale a 1-0 lead. That advantage lasted until West Scranton’s Kellan Burnside evened things up. The senior striker tallied an unassisted goal with 4:21 left in the half, sending the game to intermission with a 1-1 score. The Invaders surged into the lead less than five minutes into the second half as Maycol Gomez-Reyes notched an unassisted goal to put the visitors up 2-1. A grueling, physical slugfest ensued for the rest of the match with both teams receiving yellow cards along the way. Finally, as time ticked down in regulation, Honesdale broke through. Jase Berkihiser did the honors. The young midfielder converted a direct kick with 5:56 remaining in regulation, curling the ball beautifully into the upper right corner of the net and setting off a celebration in the stands. Berkihiser is just a sophomore, and it marked the first goal of his varsity career. The two teams then battled bitterly down the stretch, but the clock wound down to all zeroes for a 2-2 stalemate. “I’m just so proud of our senior boys and the leadership they displayed,” Rosar said. “Despite falling behind on the scoreboard, they were able to help the team keep its composure and find a way to get back into the game.” Challenges lie ahead Honesdale closed out its regular season with a league record of 5-7-2. The Hornets finished fifth in the Division II standings behind Dunmore (14-0-0), Mid Valley (9-3-2), Western Wayne (7–6-1) and Gregory the Great (5-6-3). Pairings for the District 2 Class AAA tournament will be announced on Oct. 23 with playoff action commencing Oct. 27. In all likelihood, Honesdale will enter the fray seeded sixth and draw an away match at No. 3 North Pocono. The Trojans are currently 9-4-4 with one match remaining, on the road at Wallenpaupack Area. “These kids are so excited about playoffs,” Rosar said. “We plan on playing in a way that all Hornet fans will be proud of. With a little rest and a few of our guys closer to 100 percent, we're planning on being competitive in playoffs. Don't count this team out.” This article originally appeared on Tri-County Independent: Honesdale boys soccer battles West Scranton to a draw on senior night

item.title: Next Man United manager: Who could replace Michael Carrick?
item.description: Michael Carrick is running out of time to save his job at Manchester United , with the club poised to ramp up the search for a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos took over football operations. Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – has come under huge pressure following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years and the dismal 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night. While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – Carrick’s appears to be on the brink following criticism of his tactics by the United captain Bruno Fernandes . While he is set to remain in charge for Sunday’s home game against Bournemouth , the club have already discussed potential replacements should Carrick follow the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim under the Ineos leadership. But who could United turn to as they seek to salvage their campaign? Eddie Howe The Englishman is available after his shock decision to leave Newcastle United in the summer . Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives. The 48-year-old remains highly regarded in English football after taking over a Newcastle side in the relegation zone and leading them to the club’s highest Premier League finish in two decades, as well as their first domestic silverware in 70 years. Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford. He is currently the favourite with the bookies. Howe led Newcastle to the Carabao Cup in 2025 before leaving at the end of the following season (Getty) Fabian Hurzeler Brighton have been the surprise package in the Premier League this season and the 33-year-old Hurzeler has drawn praise for turning the Seagulls into a side capable of competing with the country’s biggest clubs. Brighton’s 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal earlier this season was a masterclass in modern coaching while Hurzeler’s side also knocked United out of the Carabao Cup with a brilliant 3-2 win at Old Trafford. The Independent’s Chief Football Writer Miguel Delaney has reported that Hurzeler is admired at Old Trafford but Brighton would demand significant compensation for the highly-rated German and United may not have the cash. At Brighton, Hurzeler has also enjoyed an environment where the club have made all the right decisions off the pitch. At United, he would arguably be walking into the opposite. item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick is running out of time to save his job at Manchester United , with the club poised to ramp up the search for a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos took over football operations. Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – has come under huge pressure following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years and the dismal 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night. While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – Carrick’s appears to be on the brink following criticism of his tactics by the United captain Bruno Fernandes . While he is set to remain in charge for Sunday’s home game against Bournemouth , the club have already discussed potential replacements should Carrick follow the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim under the Ineos leadership. But who could United turn to as they seek to salvage their campaign? Eddie Howe The Englishman is available after his shock decision to leave Newcastle United in the summer . Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives. The 48-year-old remains highly regarded in English football after taking over a Newcastle side in the relegation zone and leading them to the club’s highest Premier League finish in two decades, as well as their first domestic silverware in 70 years. Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford. He is currently the favourite with the bookies. Howe led Newcastle to the Carabao Cup in 2025 before leaving at the end of the following season (Getty) Fabian Hurzeler Brighton have been the surprise package in the Premier League this season and the 33-year-old Hurzeler has drawn praise for turning the Seagulls into a side capable of competing with the country’s biggest clubs. Brighton’s 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal earlier this season was a masterclass in modern coaching while Hurzeler’s side also knocked United out of the Carabao Cup with a brilliant 3-2 win at Old Trafford. The Independent’s Chief Football Writer Miguel Delaney has reported that Hurzeler is admired at Old Trafford but Brighton would demand significant compensation for the highly-rated German and United may not have the cash. At Brighton, Hurzeler has also enjoyed an environment where the club have made all the right decisions off the pitch. At United, he would arguably be walking into the opposite. Fabian Hurzeler led Brighton to a brilliant win at Old Trafford earlier this season (Getty) Julian Nagelsmann The former wunderkind of German coaching was reportedly on United’s radar when they sacked Ruben Amorim at the start of the year, but as an option for the summer following the World Cup. Well, that was a bit of a disaster for the former Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig coach, as Germany were knocked out in the last-32 by Paraguay. Nagelsmann, 39, would naturally be interested in managing United and the club’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, previously worked with him at Red Bull. Julian Nagelsmann has been considered by United in the past and is available (Getty) Unai Emery The Spaniard has done a superb job at Aston Villa by securing Champions League qualification and ending the club’s trophy drought with victory in the Europa League. But Aston Villa will be even more determined to keep Emery given the club are only in the early stages of their rebuild under him, having completely overhauled the spine of their team over the summer. As it is, Emery enjoys complete control over his project at Villa Park, a reality he is unlikely to find at Old Trafford, while he appears enthused by the challenge of constructing a second competitive team in the Premier League. With Emery, who is under contract until 2029, United would also need to pay Villa compensation, and that may place him above their budget. Unai Emery appears enthused by the challenge of building ‘Villa 2.0’ (Getty) Antonio Conte The appeal of the combustible Italian only has grown while United have been accused of becoming too passive and pedestrian on the pitch. Conte is one of the most demanding coaches in the game and would instantly bring a level of intensity and urgency that has been lacking this season, while his CV – with Serie A titles at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli and a Premier League crown with Chelsea – commands respect. Conte also brought an immediate improvement when he took charge of a floundering Tottenham five years ago and led them back into the Champions League, which now has to be United’s biggest concern. So the 57-year-old offers impact, but then what? Conte has a sharp tongue and is not afraid to criticise his bosses if he feels they are failing to support him. His exit from Tottenham in March 2023 followed a stunning evisceration of the club in a now legendary press conference at Southampton. United would be playing with fire but options of Conte’s calibre are few and far between. United could be playing with fire if they turn to Conte (AFP/Getty) Cesc Fabregas The former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea midfielder is developing a reputation as Europe’s brightest young coach – as his brilliant Como side demonstrated by thrashing United in the Champions League on Wednesday night. The Spaniard appears committed to his project in northern Italy, though, and also has a financial incentive to continue leading Como in their debut Champions League campaign due to owning a stake in the Serie A club. The 39-year-old’s own stock is also rising and the lure of returning to one of his former clubs in the future, such as Barcelona, could result in Fabregas taking a patient and considered approach to his next move. Cesc Fabregas helped Como into the Champions League for the first time in their history after just two years in the job (Reuters) Another interim Well, we’ve been here before. Before Michael Carrick stepped into the breach in January it was Under-18s manager Darren Fletcher, who oversaw the draw with Burnley and FA Cup third-round defeat to Brighton. Before him, Ruud van Nistelrooy held the reins between Erik ten Hag’s dismissal and Amorim’s appointment and before that, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer experienced the same cycle of boom-and-bust that Carrick has gone through over the past 10 months. In short, there’s no shortage of former United players who are available to remind an underperforming dressing room of the importance of the badge and the meaning of the shirt. It could be time for Fletcher to give Sir Alex another call. Under-18s boss Darren Fletcher took charge of two games following the dismissal of Ruben Amorim in January (Getty)

item.title: 27 Years Later, Linus' Final 'Peanuts' Quote Is a Brilliant Comic Strip Callback
item.description: Charles Schulz's Peanuts , for whatever reason, has one of the more dedicated fan communities on the internet. The Peanuts Fandom wiki is an invaluable resource for anything you might want to know about the strip, from obscure characters to running jokes to the gang’s unofficial cameo appearances in later media like Family Guy . While Peanuts itself has been the subject of broad academic discussion since the end of its original run, its wiki has that dense block of exhaustive well-organized trivia that you only really get from dedicated fans. (They probably ought to get the Peanuts wiki off of Fandom at some point.)

item.title: FG intensifies response to confirmed Ebola case in FCT
item.description: The Federal Government says it has deepened public health response following the confirmation of an Ebola virus disease (EVD) case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Oct. 20, 2026. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued by Mr Oluwafemi Adeniyi, the ministry’s spokesman on Thursday. According to him, such a response to the confirmed case of the disease in the FCT is coming against the backdrop of information provided by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. Adeniyi said, “The patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda. “She was subsequently admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received medical care for several days before her diagnosis was confirmed; the patient is currently in isolation and receiving treatment.” He narrated that the government, through the Federal Ministry of Health and the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), is working with the FCT Health Services Secretariat to contain the infection and prevent further transmission. Also, that contact tracing operations had commenced with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring and appropriate public health follow-up. This, according to him, means response teams are working to identify, assess and monitor individuals who may have been exposed to the virus, including healthcare workers, patients, carers and persons linked to the patient’s travel. “Government is also coordinating surveillance, laboratory testing and other essential response activities in line with established public health protocols,” he said. He mentioned that the measures taken by government are intended to facilitate early identification of potential cases, strengthen infection prevention and control, and minimise risks of further transmission. He reiterated the government’s commitment to safeguarding the health and well-being of Nigerians and all residents, urging the public to cooperate with such moves. “Members of the public are urged to remain calm, avoid speculation and misinformation, and adhere strictly to advisories issued by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC and relevant health authorities. “The public is encouraged to rely exclusively on verified information from official government channels,” he said. He reaffirmed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would liaise with relevant national institutions and other stakeholders, as necessary, in supporting the government’s coordinated response to the public health situation. He further assured that an update would be issued through official channels, as verified information becomes available, while thanking the public and all stakeholders for their cooperation. (NAN) The post FG intensifies response to confirmed Ebola case in FCT appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: U-17 Women’s World ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌​⁠​‍‌​​‌​Cup: Flamingos face North Korea in crucial clash
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos face a stern test against defending champions Korea DPR on Friday as they seek to secure a place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Korea DPR, two-time champions since the competition began in New Zealand in 2008, have been impressive, winning their opening two matches to top Group B. The North Koreans have scored 12 goals and conceded only one, underlining their attacking strength as they pursue another title. Nigeria, bronze medallists in 2022, are seeking to keep their campaign alive after losing 2-1 to Poland before recovering with a 2-0 victory over tournament debutants Puerto Rico. The Flamingos will need a disciplined performance against the defending champions, with qualification for the knockout stage still within reach. A win or draw would guarantee Nigeria’s progress, while a defeat would leave their chances dependent on the outcome of the Poland-Puerto Rico match and the applicable tiebreakers. item.title: 2027: Atiku suffering from ‘Emir complex’ — Segun Sowunmi
item.description: Segun Sowunmi, a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of being disconnected from the struggles of ordinary Nigerians, saying he suffers from what he described as an “Emir complex”. Sowunmi made the remarks during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub , while assessing President Bola Tinubu’s chances of re-election in 2027 and responding to opposition leaders who argue that the contest will be between the ruling APC and Nigerians, regardless of the number of governors backing the president. The APC chieftain questioned the credibility of opposition figures, including Atiku and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, to speak for Nigerians grappling with poverty, given their long years in public office. He said Amaechi had spent much of his political career in government before recently positioning himself as a voice against poverty in the country. Atiku has 'Emir complex'; may Amaechi's mum flog him for politicising her death – Segun Sowunmi Watch full video here at https://t.co/AgSAGKPNoq pic.twitter.com/s39zCkBwub — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) October 23, 2026 “The opposition that all of their lives, they have just been eating from both sides of their mouths like Rotimi Amaechi, who spent the last 24 years, minus the time that they asked him to go and sit down somewhere; he has been in government, and suddenly Rotimi is the epitome that’s going to tell you that there’s poverty in Nigeria?” he asked. Sowunmi also questioned Atiku’s ability to understand the experiences of poor Nigerians, pointing to his time as vice president under former President Olusegun Obasanjo from 1999 to 2007 and his public profile. “Up till today, Atiku was vice president 1999 to 2007, that’s when he stopped his vice presidency,” he said. Describing what he called an “Emir complex”, Sowunmi argued that Atiku’s lifestyle and public demeanour made it difficult for him to empathise with people struggling to make ends meet. “Up till today, have you seen vice president that goes around the way Atiku is going around with convoy, in terms of his panache, Atiku is suffering from what you call an Emir complex,” he said. Explaining the phrase, Sowunmi said it referred to a powerful figure accustomed to being treated with deference by people around him. “You know what an Emir complex is? That big man that everybody will just come and say, ‘Dan labayi; ranka dede;’ or an oba complex,” he said. He added that Atiku was not qualified to present himself as a champion of the poor. “So he has no capacity to know or empathise with the poor. He is not a patron deity of the poor,” Sowunmi said. The APC campaign council member maintained that the opposition’s criticism of Tinubu and his administration should be assessed against the records of those making the claims. Tinubu is seeking another term in 2027, with APC governors and some governors elected on other party platforms among those

item.title: Asian Football Confederation backs Gianni Infantino in U-turn on Fifa presidency
item.description: AFC president Sheikh Salman praises and hugs Infantino It had stood with Uefa and Concacaf against him The Asian Football Confederation has endorsed Gianni Infantino for another term as Fifa’s president in a turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s world governing body for a breach of trust. The AFC president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement. Continue reading...
